SibiTalent did not comment on the media as of the time of the publication (source: Stuffing Industries Analysts, 2026-10-05).

---

Can employers request H-1B identity? Where are the legal boundaries?

This is the most confusing problem for many students in search of work.Brief answer: Visa status may not be a condition for screening.

Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 prohibitsNationalityDiscrimination in employment. EEOC ' s enforcement position is that the use of visa types as recruitment filters is almost equivalent in practice to the use of nationality as a criterion and constitutes proxy discrimination (proxy discrimination).

In an official statement, the President of EEOC, Andrea Lucas, stated:

"Employers and employment agents cannot exclude qualified Americans out of employment by using us as an alternative to nationality discrimination."

Illegal border references:

OperationLegalityAnnotations
Require candidates to have legal working authorization before they are on dutyLegalCommon work acquisition requirements
"Only H-1B" "No OPT" "No CPT"The risk of breaking the law is extremely high.In lieu of nationality discrimination by type of visa
Note "No visa guarantee"Gray zoneUsually allowed by the court, but subject to the context
Prioritization of candidates of specific nationalities:: Violation of the lawOne of the core charges in the Sibit case
Ask the candidate when the job authorization expiresBe careful.No grounds for discrimination

---

What does this case mean for OPT/H-1B students seeking employment?

The discrimination victim in this case is an American citizen, but the market phenomenon it reveals is as important to OPT and H-1B holders as it is to US citizens.

There are two opposites that you may encounter:

Scenario 1: you have OPT, but the recruiter only has H-1B This indicates that some employers are in breach of the law. You have the right to complain to EEOC, especially when the recruiter expressly rejects you with a visa and you are qualified accordingly.

Scenario 2: You have H-1B, but the job market is "hidden H-1B". The SibiTalent case revealed the usual operation of the IT manpower outsourcing industry - giving priority to the selection of candidates who already have H-1B, since the customer is not required to pay the cost of the visa guarantee. This would be in your interest in the short term, but there is a high risk of long-term reliance on such intermediaries: such companies are in doubt about compliance and may face legal problems affecting your employer ' s qualifications at any time.

Practical advice for students to seek employment:

  • Avoid Only H-1BSuch companies are at high risk of compliance and may be implicated in your visa status once prosecuted or closed.
  • Prioritize large employers with sponsorship recordsReference is made to the USCIS publicly available H-1B employer database, giving priority to companies with historical records.
  • Receipt of discriminatory mail, maintenance of intercepts: If you are an American citizen or a Green Card holder receives an email similar to "Only H-1B", you can submit a complaint online to EEOC (eeeoc.gov).
  • Inner Push > IntermediariesThe most effective way to circumvent visa bias is through bypassing third-party manpower companies, direct contact with Hiring Manager through alumni networks, LinkedIn.

---

Common problems

Did the recruitment company say "Only H-1B" is illegal? According to EEOC's prosecution position, yes. This case (3:2026 cv 11106) is typical of the fact that the type of visa used as the selection criterion for recruitment is recognized under federal law as potentially constituting discrimination on the basis of nationality.

I have OPT, and the employer says, "Don't supply sponsorship," is that legal? It is usually legal. The expression "no visa guarantee" is different from "no visa status, as long as the employer defines its own cost boundaries and is not explicitly qualified as discrimination by EEOC.

Can I trust the H-1B broker's recommendation? A careful assessment is required. The SibiTalent case showed systemic compliance problems with some IT manpower outsourcing companies. In selecting an intermediary, priority is given to verifying whether it has a formal employer guarantee record and an EEOC complaint history.

Does my H-1B employer's being sued by EEOC affect my visa status? The litigation itself does not automatically render H-1B invalid, but if the employer closes or is disqualified for an offence, your visa will lose its attachment and a new sponsor will need to be found and submitted as soon as possible. It is recommended that migrant lawyers be consulted in a timely manner.

How do students find jobs to circumvent visa bias? Intropolation is the most effective way. Directly through an alumni or Hiring Manager, your abilities can be seen before the employer makes an official visa assessment.

ice-cpt-0q5gf.title: ICE suddenly changed the rules! The CPT has been sued by various universities.
ice-cpt-0q5gf.dek: ICE suddenly tightened the CPT policy in August 2026, resulting in a number of university internships called " Staying Students " , and the Union of Universities of Higher Education has officially challenged.
ice-cpt-0q5gf.body:
In August 2026, ICE (United States Bureau of Immigration and Customs Enforcement) suddenly tightened the criteria for the qualification of CPT employment, which directly led to the suspension of practical training programmes for students in some higher education institutions. In early October 2026, the Association of American Universities, among others, jointly filed a lawsuit with the Federal District Court of Massachusetts against ICE for violating the Administrative Procedure Act. For Chinese students with F-1 visas seeking employment in the United States, this was one of the most immediate migration policy developments in 2026.

---

Key points

  • ICE suddenly changed the CPT eligibility criteria in August 2026.This was not sufficiently explained and there was a significant departure from past policies.
  • The U.S. Association of Universities and Colleges and others filed a federal suit in October 2026.The ICE Directive was found to be contrary to the Administrative Procedure Act and the procedure was unlawful.
  • Some universities have suspended relevant CPT training projectsF-1 students directly dependent on CPT internships.
  • CPT and OPT are the two most important forms of legal work authorization for F-1 students.Policy tightening has implications for both students and students in school.
  • The outcome of the legal proceedings is still pendingIn the short term, students are faced with high policy uncertainty and are advised to take the initiative to set up a number of job paths.

---

ICE, Tighten up the CPT policy.

In August 2026, ICE suddenly changed its official position on "what type of employment meets the CPT qualifications", according to the petition of the American University Association and others.Insufficient policy basis or transitional arrangements。

The core allegations of the indictment include:

  • ICE's new directive is a procedural requirement for public review of major policy adjustments under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA).
  • The directives directly led to the suspension of some of the existing CPT practical training programmes at the tertiary level and the consequent disruption of student internship/employment arrangements.
  • Proceedings filed in October 2026Federal District Court of Massachusetts, United States（US District Court for the District of Massachusetts）。

Currently ICE has not made public the full text of the new determination criteria, the specific implications of which remain to be determined by the Court or further clarified by ICE.

---

What's the difference between CPT and OPT? How does policy tightening affect me?

CPT and OPT are the two core mandates of F-1 students to work legally in the United States, but the trigger conditions, application process, and risk points vary.

DimensionsCPT（Curricular Practical Training）OPT（Optional Practical Training）
Phase of applicationDuring reading (directly linked to course)12 months before or after graduation
AuthorSchool DSO direct approval without USCIS approvalTo apply to USCIS for EAD card
LengthNo uniform ceiling depending on the course schedule (but full of 1 year Full-time CPT impact OPT qualification)12 months; STEM may apply for extension to 36 months
Policy implicationsDirect impact.: ICE Tightened "Qualified" employment typeWhile no direct tightening has been announced, the overall policy environment has become more stringent
Main risksSchool suspension. Internship interrupted; qualification retroactively invalid.EAD Extension of approval cycle; STEM OPT renewal uncertainty
Suggested ActionsConfirm project status immediately with DSO/International OfficeEarly submission of applications and retention of all work-learning certificates

The most direct impact on students in ChinaStudents who rely on CPT to complete their internships during their studies or who are working as CPT must contact the School International Student Office (DSO) to confirm whether the project has been affected.

---

Why would the university sue ICE?

The core legal argument of the college union is:Procedural irregularitiesInstead of simply opposing the content of the policy itself.

Under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), federal agencies are generally required to:

  1. Publication of proposed rules (Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, NPRM)
  2. Open public comment period (usually 60 days)
  3. Formal entry into force only after written responses to comments

According to the plaintiff, ICE jumped out of these steps this time.Arbitrary administrative acts(Arbitrary and capricious), therefore not procedurally valid.

Legal resultsSuch APA proceedings have historically been upheld by the courts (e.g. 2017 DACA-related proceedings). wandover-wk42l.title: How many audits have been cut down? AI's on duty. Can we get in with the students?
wandover-wk42l.dek: Big Four is reshaping the Graduate training system, AI is replacing a large number of entry-level compliance missions, traditional audit corridors are narrow and how can students be accommodated?
wandover-wk42l.body:
In 2026, KPMG, Deloitte, EY, PwC, four of the world's largest professional services, fully re-engineered their graduate training system - – AI is taking over the task of entry-level compliance, such as data entry, invoice validation, basic reports, which was previously performed by students, and new recruits face complex judgemental work. For North American Chinese students who are applying for four major internships or full-time positions, this means that the traditional "audit line" has become narrower and needs to be adjusted as quickly as possible in terms of skill structures and job-seeking strategies.

---

Key points

  • The four majors have fully adapted the Graduate training in 2026As AI takes over repetitive tasks such as data extraction, basic abnormalities testing, new arrivals are pushed into complex judgement settings earlier.
  • The head of the EY talent said publicly"Problems, critical reasoning and teamwork" are becoming a higher priority for recruitment than technical operations.
  • KPMG introduced "Launch Pad" assessment dayThe focus is on resilience (resilient), resilience (adaptability) and relationship construction, rather than purely GPS and mathematical tests.
  • PwC mandatory debate trainingSimulation of high-pressure client interaction requires that newcomers be able to articulate complex financial perspectives and defend professional judgement.
  • There's been a contraction in the overall gradiute intake.However, the four main groups continue to invest in talent development — more demanding and competitive posts left behind.

---

Who's the big four? What's the logical change?

According to Straamline Feed, released on 23 September 2026, the four major focus of recruitment assessment has shifted from academic achievement to behavioural and soft skills.

Logical comparison of recruitment (by 2023 vs. 2026):

DimensionsTraditional models (2023 years)AI Age Model (2026)
Main responsibilities in first gradeManual data entry, invoice validation, base contract extractionReview of exception reports generated by AI, early client advisory, complex judgement applications
Core skills developmentExcel operation speed and accuracy, program complianceCritical reasoning, prompt engagement, professional doubts about algorithm output
Human skills trainingMainly for observation purposes - follow the senior manager to attend client meetingsActive communication training camps, structured debates, simulation of client negotiations
Priorities for the evaluation of recruitmentAccomplishments + Standard Mathematical Logic TestAdaptiveness, resilience, teamwork, behavioural questions Answer

This shift has a direct impact on students: The GPS is no longer a decisive advantage, and the ability to present "humans are irreplaceable" with limited work experience is key to screening.

---

What's "Apprenticeship Gap"? What does it mean for students to seek employment?

The "apprenticeship Gap" mentioned in the original version is one of the four major internal structural risks:

  • In the past, thousands of hours of repetitive work helped Junior staff to build a particle-level understanding of client operations, and "intuitiveness" formed in a repetition.
  • Now AI has crossed this base, and newcomers are required to make high-level professional judgements directly without sufficient experience.
  • Four are trying to "man-made" the missing experience through debate sessions, scenario simulations, coaching.

For a student.: When you get to the top four, there will be no buffer period for "one year of simple work first" From the first day onwards, there is a need to demonstrate the ability of the client to communicate. Without advance preparation, adaptation curves are very steep.

---

How can students adapt their strategies to avoid being eliminated in 2026?

In the face of four major structural transformations, the following are immediate directions of action:

1. Skills upgrading: additional AI-related competencies, not just "know Excel"

  • Learning Data Analysis Tool (Python / SQL / Power BI) and combined with the audit scene
  • To understand the practical application of AI in the area of compliance (e.g., abnormality detection, classification of documents) and to be able to present specific scenarios during interviews
  • Mastering basic prompt engineering, which has been clearly identified as new skills

2. Enhancement of "human Skills" with documented cases in interviews

  • Preparation of 3-5 STAR stories reflecting critical reasoning, cross-sectoral collaboration, high-pressure decision-making
  • Participation in projects with customer communication attributes (case competitions, negotiation project, simulation negotiations)

3. Early establishment of internal referral corridor Four campus recruitments are increasingly dependent on internal referrals for filtering curricula vitae. Access to active staff six to nine months prior to the application period is key to accessing the curriculum vitae.

4. Consider moving from an advisory direction to a non-traditional audit line Data analysis (DA), risk counselling, ESG compliance, etc. are relatively less affected by AI and the four main directions are still expanding.

---

Common problems

Are the students still enrolled in 2026? Yes, the four main groups continue to invest in the gradiute culture, but the overall intake scale has contracted due to macroeconomic pressures and automation. The remaining posts are more competitive and students need to be prepared earlier and more precisely.

What specific entry-level jobs did AI automate? According to September 2026 reports, the main automation included data extraction, invoice validation (ticking and testing), base contract interpretation, and the generation of preliminary abnormality reports. These were the core routines of the first year of Junior Auditor.

What's going on in the four interviews? Does the GPA matter? KPMG, among others, has clearly revised the GPS weight downwards to give greater weight to daaptability (adaptability), resilience (pressure resistance), teamwork and behaviour scenario performance. Academic achievement remains the threshold, but is no longer the main distinguishing dimension.

How can a student with little work experience demonstrate the ability of "humans to be irreplaceable"? Who needs to pay the $100,000? Who's exempt?

For most Chinese students studying in the United States, studying through OPT or Cap-Exempt, $100,000 is currently spentIt's not a direct obstacle.I don't know. If you have left the country and need to re-enter the country to activate H-1B, you need to be particularly careful.

Has the court stopped the fee? What's the legal status?

This is the most complex and interesting part of the story.

Timeline combing:

TimeEvents

June 2026The District Court of Massachusetts ruled that the claim was contrary to the law and revoked the relevant government action.
24 July 2026The First Circuit Court of Appeals denied the Government ' s request for a stay of the original judgement, and the original decision continued.

Core ContrastThe Federal Court had found that the fee was unlawful, but the Government had chosen to appeal and continue to defer the notice. In other words, the White House issued a moratorium, but the Court ' s decision is still valid. Uncertainty exists at the practical level of enforcement pending appeals. 1. Active promotion of H-1B drawing of lots during OPT Currently, OPT holders apply for H-1B in the United States, which is not covered by $100,000. Using the OPT (and STEM OPT) window period is the most robust route to circumvent barriers to entry abroad.

2. Avoiding unnecessary departures When holding a state of H-1B or H-1B pending, it is not necessary to leave the country for re-entry, which could trigger a scenario requiring an employer to pay $100,000. In case of travel, migrant lawyers must be consulted in advance to assess risks.

3. Costs of early communication with employers If you are recruited from abroad and need to enter the country to activate H-1B, it must be made clear at the offer negotiation stage whether the employer is willing to contribute $100,000 (after the legal situation has stabilized). Large science and technology companies and financial institutions usually have greater affordability.

4. Focus on the outcome of legal proceedings The direction of the decisions of the First Circuit Court of Appeals and the DC Circuit Court will determine whether the expenses were actually executed by September 2027. The Government has filed an appeal against the District Court ' s decision, and the extension announcement is still being advanced at the administrative level during the appeal. Final enforcement depends on the outcome of the Court of Appeal ' s decision, which is now in a legal grey area.

The drawing of lots is not directly affected by $100,000 per se, but the cost considerations of employers when hiring candidates abroad may affect their willingness to nominate them, thereby indirectly affecting the drawing of lots for some candidates.

wandover-mcnse.dek: An executive order dated 18 September issued by Trump, under which employers of layoffs would scrutinize H1B applications at a new cost of $100,000, must be placed ahead of schedule.
wandover-mcnse.body:
On 18 September 2026, Trump signed an executive decree requiring the Ministry of Labour, the State Department and the Department of Homeland Security to include in their examination of applications for H-1B labour conditions (LCA) and visa applications the employer ' s recent or planned layoffs. Meanwhile, for some new applications $100,000 H-1B surchargeAlso renewed. This means that the difficulties of H-1B sponsorship for Chinese students who are seeking employment or holding OPT are substantially increasing.

---

Key points

  • The executive order was signed.: Effective 18 September 2026, the three departments (Labour / State / Department of Homeland Security) will jointly review the downsizing records of the H-1B employer.
  • $100,000 Additional cost continuation PeriodThis fee, originally introduced in September 2025, has been renewed but is currently before the Federal Court of Appeal.
  • Retrenchment automatically refuses to sign.: An executive order does not prohibit a company from reducing its staff before sponsoring H-1B, but requires an approving officerProactive inclusion of downsizing records as a review factor。
  • Large plants and outsourcing companies are under the greatest pressure• Technology, outsourcing industries are the focus of attention, and there is a significant increase in risk from IT/outsourcing-type employer sponsorship.
  • The student should plan as early as possible. Plan B.OPT extensions, green card paths, multiple employers synchronized applications are the basic risk hedge strategy in the current environment.

---

What does this executive order specify?

On 18 September 2026, Trump signed an executive decree, the core measures being:

  1. Joint sectoral reviewsThe Department of State, the Department of Labour and the Department of Homeland Security, when processing H-1B LCA, I-129 applications and visas, are required to examine the employer ' s recent or planned lay-offs.
  2. Ministry of Labour.Data review of previously submitted LCAs will be conducted to determine whether further action against sponsored employers is required by law.
  3. Data sharing in five sectorsLabour, Homeland Security, the State Department, the Ministry of Commerce, the Ministry of Education and the Small Business Administration will share data on salaries, conditions of employment, industry and job specialization.
  4. Focus on combating violationsThe Government has named employers who are suspected of violations such as "false job descriptions, false reporting of working conditions, false pay".
Source: The American Bazaar, 20 September 2026.

---

$100,000 H-1B surcharge is still being implemented?

ItemDetails
Amount of cost$100,000 (partly new H-1B application applicable)
First Introduction TimeSeptember 2025 (Trump Government Gazette)
2026 StatusIt has been renewed by presidential proclamation and continues to be valid.
Legal challengesThe Federal Court of Appeal is reviewing its earlier decision to block the fee (as reported by Reuters)
Exempted populationExisting H-1B holders and specific covered groups, treated according to existing rules

Bottom: $100,000 surcharge is still in force, but the legal results have not yet been finalized and the way forward requires continued attention.

---

What kind of company H-1B has the highest risk of sponsoring?

The Executive Decree clearly identified two types of enterprises as the focus of attention:

High-risk type

  • Large-scale downsizing and H-1B applications filed(scientific, financial, scientific)
  • IT Outsourcing and manpower outsourcing companiesThe White House directly quoted in its executive order the alleged replacement of American employees with low-paid foreign employees.
  • Almost 12 months, any employer with a "similar position" cut record.

Relatively stable type

  • Traditional financial institutions (e.g. Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, etc.) have never experienced large-scale layoffs.
  • Companies whose core business relies on highly specialized positions (quant, SDE, data scientific)
  • A mature employer has been established to improve the H-1B compliance record
This does not mean that large plants could not be sponsored at all, but the approval cycle and the RFE (complementary evidence request) probability will increase significantly.

---

How should students now plan H-1B and alternative paths?

Policy tightening does not amount to a total H-1B closure, but waiting is the most dangerous strategy. The following is a list of core actions in the current environment:

Short term (0-3 months)

  • Confirms whether the current employer has been retrenching in size for almost two years.
  • Verification of OPT / STEM OPT validity and remaining days (unemployment period: Standard OPT unemployment ceiling 90 days, STEM OPT 150 days)
  • Early contact 2027 FY H-1B registration cycle (usually in March of the following year)

Medium (3-12 months)

  • Synchronize contact with a number of potential sponsors. Don't put eggs in a company.
  • Explore O-1A (visa for outstanding talent) as an alternative path for highly skilled personnel
  • EB-2 / EB-3 start-up window as early as possible with employers if green card is willing

Long term

  • Consider traditional financial/advisory firms with a low risk of internal staff reductions and a strong H-1B compliance record
  • Assessment of alternative markets, such as Canada/United Kingdom, as risk scenarios for career paths Charge!

More and more of the trainees we mentored began at the OPT stage with the simultaneous deployment of more than two willing employers and were screened through genuine refractions, one of the most effective risk reduction strategies in the current policy environment.

---

Common problems

When the executive order is signed, will my search for work during OPT be affected? OPT itself is not directly affected by this executive order, but if your target employer has a recent staff reduction record, the probability that they will be subjected to RFE or rejected when they submit an H-1B application for you. It is recommended that priority be given to companies with a clean history of downsizing.

$100,000 H-1B. Is the surcharge for all applicants? Nope. This fee applies to "part of the new H-1B application", and the existing H-1B holders and specific covered groups are treated in accordance with the differential rules. The specific scope of application suggests access to the latest bulletin of the USCIS network or consultation with immigration lawyers.

The employer can't make me H-1B when I'm laid off. The executive order does not prohibit post-retrenchment sponsorship, but requires the approving officer as an important review factor. In other words, redundancy does not amount to automatic refusal, but significantly increases the difficulty and time of vetting, and employers need to provide fuller documentation.

IT, outsourcing company H-1B, is it completely useless? Current policy exerts the strongest pressure on outsourced employers, but "no" is an exaggeration. The actual impact is a longer processing time, an increased frequency of RFEs, and more difficult access to some low-paid jobs. For STEM OPT-enabled students, the risk of outsourcing company-sponsored pathways does increase substantially.

If the H-1B policy continues to tighten, is O-1A a realistic option? O-1A is a real and viable path for people with the highest published papers, well-known competition awards or proven contributions within the industry. It is relatively stable without drawing lots, but the material preparation threshold is high and requires 6-12 months of advance planning.

What's the difference between CPT and OPT? wandover-gfcfj.title: The court just stopped! Trump's four-year visa limit. The students won.
wandover-gfcfj.dek: On 15 September, the Federal Court issued a nationwide injunction preventing Trump from bringing into force the new four-year reduction of the student visa to four years, while OPT and the school window were temporarily maintained.
wandover-gfcfj.body:
On 15 September 2026, the United States Federal Court issued a national interim injunction (TRO) to prevent the Trump Government from formally limiting the validity of F-1 student visas (and J visas) to four years of new land. The ban, which was issued on 14 September by Dennis Saylor, a judge of the Federal District Court of Massachusetts, came into effect immediately throughout the United States, meaning that the existing system of Duration of Status (validity of identity) for Chinese students was maintained for the time being and OPT internship windows were not subject to immediate shocks.

---

Key points

  • The national ban is in force.On 14 September 2026, Dennis Saylor, Justice of the Boston Federal Court, issued an interim injunction to suspend the new regulation throughout the United States and not limited to a particular state.
  • The original rule was overturned.: Trump Government intends to limit the maximum period of residence of F-1 student visas and J exchange visit visas to a single period. 4 yearsI Visa (foreign journalist) restricted to 240 days。
  • Other OrganiserThe current system allows students to stay legally while they continue to engage in activities consistent with the purposes of entry (e.g. study, research, OPT internships) without additional application for extension.
  • Justification of the CourtThe judge found that the policy changes provided by DHS were "extremely weak" and did not adequately assess the damage and did not consider less restrictive alternatives.
  • Impact on job search for studentsIf the new regulations enter into force, Ph.D. students, five-year undergraduate students and OPT/STEM OPT students will face a mandatory reduction in the U.S. time window; the pressure will be temporarily lifted upon landing of the ban.

---

What's the new four-year Trump student visa?

The Trump government introduced new rules through the DHS, and the core change was to abolish the last 50 years. Duration of Status（D/S） The system was changed to a rigid ceiling for visa residence:

Type of visaCurrent systemNew regulations
F-1 (international students)"Duration of Status, continued validity during studyMaximum 4 yearsOverdue request for extension
J (Exchange Visiting Scholar)Duration of StatusMaximum 4 years
I (foreign journalist)Duration of StatusMaximum 240 days

The new rule was originally 15 September 2026 Entry into force. If landed, students and scholars wishing to remain in the United States for more than four years would have to apply to the USCIS and be granted extensions, the process would significantly increase the administrative burden and uncertainty.

Judge Saylor noted, inter alia, that undergraduate projects in the United States usually take more than four years to complete, that doctoral programmes take longer and that a one-size-fits-all four-year cap would directly disrupt the academic programmes of a large number of students. He also quoted calculations from research universities such as Harvard University and MIT: If the new regulations come into effect, a drop in enrolment and an increase in administrative costs will result in losses to American universities. Hundreds of millions of dollars。

---

Why did the courts issue national interim injunctions? What's the impact on OPT?

Judge Saylor has three central reasons for the injunction:

  1. Irregular proceduresDHS provides an "extremely weak" legal basis for such a significant policy change without adequate due process review.
  2. Insufficient damage assessment: The Government has not adequately assessed the potential harm of the policy to students, universities and the United States economy, nor has it considered less restrictive alternatives.
  3. Historic contributions ignoredThe current system has enabled tens of millions of foreign students and researchers to study in the United States over the past 50 years and has contributed significantly to United States research and economic development.

Direct impact on Chinese students seeking employment:

  • Short term (in the period of entry into force of the ban): Maintenance of the status quo ante of the Duration of Status system and no impact on the legality of residence of students with F-1 visas during OPT/STEM OPT internships.
  • STEM OPT ExtensionUnder the current system, STEM OPT can be extended to 36 months, and this window continues to apply during the prohibition period.
  • H-1B Transition period for drawing of lots: OPT transition time window (Cap-Gap) to H-1B is not compressed for the time.
  • Medium- and long-term uncertaintyThe interim injunction is not a permanent ruling, the DHS may amend the rules to be resubmitted or appealed, and the policy direction still requires continued attention.

It is noteworthy that this is not an isolated case where the policy of the Trump Government has been blocked in court. According to the newspaper, only the proceedings relating to the First Amendment were concerned, and federal judges have ruled in 75 cases that the actions of the second government of Trump were unconstitutional or illegal. In addition, in June 2026, the Federal Court found illegal the measure of charging $100,000 for the company ' s new H-1B work visa and found that the Government was not entitled to levy substantial new taxes without Congress ' approval.

---

What does this mean for the 2026 time line for students seeking employment?

For Chinese students who are seeking employment in the United States, the ban provides the following breathing space at the job search rhythm:

Current timeline reference (Autumn 2026)

Employment stageKey NodesLinks to visa policy

H-1B FY2027 registrationMarch 2027 (projected)Cap-Gap protects windows from compression
STEM OPT application90 days before graduationThe 36-month extension window was temporarily retained
Final decision on policy litigationUnknown (possibly 2027)There's still uncertainty about the end result.

Recommendations:

  • (a) Early access to full-time offer to reduce reliance on the length of the OPT window;
  • Maintaining communication with the International Student Office (DSO) of the school and monitoring the renewal of the I-20;
  • Concerned about USCIS (uscis.gov) and DHS official announcements and whether DHS has resubmitted the rules;
  • Target companies with H-1B capacity and priority delivery (Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Meta, Google, Amazon, etc. have stable sponsor records).

---

Common problems

I'm holding an F-1 visa now. Will four-year restrictions affect me? Not at the moment. The national interim injunction of the Federal Court came into force on 15 September 2026, and the new regulations were completely suspended, and your status of Duration of Status remained valid for the duration of the injunction without an additional request for an extension to the USCIS.

What is the difference between an interim injunction and a permanent ruling? What about the follow-up? The interim injunction (TRO), which is a provisional measure of the court during the hearing of the case, prevents the rule from coming into force immediately, but is not final. DHS may be resubmitted after appeal or amendment of the rules, and it is suggested that ongoing attention be paid to notices of USCIS (uscis.gov) and school DSO.

Is the 36-month extension of STEM OPT still valid? Effective. The STEM OPT extension system, which is governed by independent legislation, has been suspended under the new four-year residence cap, and the STEM OPT application process is currently unaffected.

What if the new rules come into effect again? If the new rules are finally laid down, the students of the Ph.D. project (usually 5-7 years) will have to apply to the USCIS for an extension after the fourth year. This is one of the damages highlighted by the litigant in this case, and the Court also justified the injunction.

Does this ban affect H-1B applications? Indirectly beneficial. OPT identity stability means that the Cap-Gap protection window is not compressed and the time buffer left to candidates to complete the H-1B drawing of lots and approval is retained. In addition, $100,000 H-1B additional costs were found to be in breach of the law by the Federal Court in June 2026.

usc-cpt-27ew0.body:

---

Why did USC CPT suddenly tighten in 2026?

On 12 August and 24 August 2026, two successive CPT guidance memorandums were issued by SEVP (Student and Exchange Victor Programme) of ICE. The core logic is one thing:

The CPT must be the indispensable, if not the completed, part of the graduated CPT, rather than an optional course for temporary work permits.

In the original version of the SEVP memorandum of August 24, the CPT is allowed only when "training is an important part of an accomplished curriculum".

This Article directly hits the most common CPT operating path in the past:

  1. Find an internship.
  2. Registering an Intership Active Course (e.g. ENGR 596/597/598)
  3. CPT School

The problem is that if this class is just elective, students can graduate without an internship -- it's hard to prove that physical training is the "must part" of degree requirement.

Direct consequences：

  • UC Berkeley Pause Course Credit CPT
  • UCSD suspended processing of CPT applications
  • USC from 24 August explicitly approve only the corresponding CPT
  • Penn suspended all CPT applications in August until 10 September I've only announced the resumption of federal applications.

---

USC Viterbi, what is the new CPT process?

The USC strategy is not to wait for policy to be relaxed, but to modify the curriculum to conform to the new rules. From 2026 Fall, adopted 2026-27 Catalogue The new CPT path is as follows:

StepsAction itemRemarks
1Find an internship.Same as before
2Confirm meeting 2026-27 Catalogue requirementsUndergraduate: ENGR 495; MA/PHD: ENGR 595
3Registering for Engineering PracticeThe lesson has been written to
4Corporate Corporation CompletionInvolving Employer, Internship Supervisor and School
5Application to USC OIS CPTOIS Review of immigration eligibility
6CPT Starts internship after approvalCan't take up a job until approved

Key changesIt used to be "internships, back-to-back classes," and now "the training programme itself requires completion of the physical training" — in the reverse order and logic.

The same logic was confirmed by Penn ISSS director Rudie Altamirano in his statement of 10 September: "is treated for all restorations in the academic program or track and is an integral part of the occupied territory" and the request has to be met.

---

What about old students and students who have enrolled in old classes?

This is currently the most searchable issue and the easiest place to step on.

Catalogue Year is a student of 2026-27.: Go directly to the new Practicum, as shown above.

Before Catalogue Year's continuing students：

  • Viterbi's current offer is:Voluntary Switch to 2026-27 Catalogue
  • Switch to enter ENGR 495/595 system to meet CPT requirements again
  • ⚠️ Academic Advisor must confirm before switching.– Catalogue changed, other curriculum requirements, degree requirement, graduation plan could change together.

Students enrolled in ENGR 596/597/598：

  • These courses may still count in the future.
  • But...It's a credit card.
  • Need to re-identify with OIS and Academic Advisor

Fall 2026 CPT approved before August 24th will not be revokedThis group of students is eligible for regular admission.

---

Common problems

USC CPT 2026 Fall, can you apply? Yes, but a new path must be followed: registration of ENGR 495 (undergraduate) or ENGR 595 (Master/PhD) and completion of the Internship Cooperation Agreement.

What's the difference between ENGR 595 and the original ENGR 596/597/598? ENGR 595 is Engineering Practice, officially written in 2026-27 Catalogue degre requirement; ENGR 596/597/598 is elective, which calculates credits but no longer meets the CPT's "required curriculum" requirement.

Does the senior need to change Catalogue to continue applying for CPT? Not necessarily, but if you want to take the new ENGR 495/595, switch to 2026-27 Catalogue is the current Viterbi scheme. Before switching, you must confirm with Academic Advisor the change in graduation requirements and not blindly change Catalogue for CPT.

Is it from the company or from the students? The agreement, which involves Employer, Internship Supervisor and the school, is largely carried out with the cooperation of the internship company and students need to promote formal partnerships between employers and Viterbi, a process more complex than before.

Do other schools follow up on USC's changes? It's possible. Penn announced on September 10th that it would resume the CPT treatment that meets the federal requirements, with the same requirement. The USC Viterbi model of "Booking internships into training programmes" is considered to be a more sustainable solution in the current policy environment, and the follow-up by other schools deserves continued attention.

After getting an offer, a lot of students are afraid to talk about pay, often because they don't know the market, or because they're afraid they won't. The LHH pay guide just solved the first problem -- with authoritative market-based data, it went from "I think" to "data."

Is AI really going to raise salaries by 56%? According to LHH 2027, AI currently has a pay premium of 56 per cent in the North American workplace (wage premium). But the premium applies to candidates who can clearly demonstrate and quantify AI applications, rather than simply writing "ChatGPT."

h-1b-4000-9-qmh0u.body:
United States H-1B work visa effective 9 September 20269-11 Reponse and Biometric Entry-Exit Fee (bioidentification fee) were extended to all H-1B renewal applicationsincluding renewal of the place of origin without change by the employer and additional payment per employer $4,000I don't know. Key points

---

What's the new $4,000 rule?

The new regulations do not create new costs or increase the amount, but rather expand the scope of "who has to pay".

As previously explained by DHS, the 9-11 biometric recognition fee applies mainly in two cases: the initial application for H-1B or a transfer involving a change of employer. The new rules issued on 10 August 2026 clearly state:Even if the worker remains at the same employer, the application for renewal is also subject to payment。

Type of applicationWhether contributions are required before the new regulationsWhether the new regulations require contributions
H-1B Initial applicationYeah.Yeah.

H-1B Extension of the same employerNo✅ Yes (new)
L-1 Initial applicationYeah.Yeah.
L-1 Extension of the same employerNo✅ Yes (new)
Small employers (%)<50 per cent H/L)Not applicableNot applicable

DHS states in the Federal Gazette that this is intended to support federal enforcementBiometric Entry-Exit Recording Systemand related national security functions.

---

What kind of employers are affected? What does it mean for students to seek employment?

The trigger threshold is clear: 50 United States employees and over 50 per cent are H-1B/L-1A/L-1B holders.

This threshold is precisely directed at large S & T outsourcing companies (e.g. Infosys, Cognizant, Wipro, etc., Indian IT companies) and enterprises that rely in part on foreign engineers. For the common job-seeking objectives of Rexpand trainees - Google, Meta, Amazon, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, etc. - Since the proportion of foreign workers is usually not more than 50 per cent,Probably not directly covered by this new regulation. Internal。

However, this does not mean that students in China can be completely excluded. The following are of concern:

  • Pay negotiations may narrow down.The cost of H-1B sponsorship by the affected employer is increased by $4,000 per renewal, and, although direct pay deductions are prohibited by law, the overall labour-budget pressure of the employer increases, which may affect salary increases or headcount decisions.
  • Declining willingness of small and medium-sized employers to sponsor: For medium-sized companies that happen to trigger the threshold, an additional $4,000 per renewal may justify a reduction in the H-1B slot.
  • Active confirmation of employer sponsorship policy when seeking employmentAt the interview or offer negotiation stage, it is recommended that companies be directly asked whether they bear the full cost of visas and the renewal policy.

Timeline at Cost

Critical Time NodesEvents

30 September 2027Deadline for application under current rules

The direct impact of this new regulation is limited for Chinese students who are in the OPT or STEM OPT stage and are ready to smoke H-1B, but background pressures cannot be ignored.

  • H-1B drawing of lots is not per se affectedNo change in the cost of the drawing of lots for registration ($215) and other USCIS applications, and $4,000 for biometric recognition only for specific employers that meet the threshold.
  • You have to do your homework when you choose to sponsor your employer.Priority is given to large mainstream STI/FIN companies with less than 50 per cent of foreign employees, avoiding outsourcing companies that trigger the threshold because of the high proportion of foreign employees, which in itself also helps to get better offers.
  • Inner push is still the key to breaking the game.In the larger context of rising costs of employer sponsorship, employers' concerns about H-1B sponsorship are reduced more than those of the CV, by pushing directly into the interview process and shortening the recruitment cycle.

Of the Rexpand tutors, throughLinkedIn Insport + Email InspectorThe percentage of interview opportunities is significantly higher than pure Internet applications, and the number of offers obtained covers Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Google, Meta, Amazon, etc. - The H-1B sponsorship policy of these companies is relatively stable and less affected by the new regulations.

Is $4,000 paid by me or by the employer? By the employer. DHS expressly states that the H-1B employer may not transfer the fee to H-1B employees by way of a reduction in salary, deduction of benefits or any other means.

I'm holding H-1B. Will this new rule affect my next renewal? If your employer meets the threshold of "50 U.S. employees and more than 50% H/L visa holders", your request for renewal will trigger $4,000 at the employer's expense. If the employer does not meet the threshold, it will not be affected.

When will the new rules expire? According to the Federal Gazette, the current rules apply to applications submitted before 30 September 2027. Follow-up to the DHS is a matter of concern.

What is the cost of the L-1 visa? The L-1 applicable employer must pay each application $4,500It also extends to renewal applications from the same employer.

Is this new rule the same as the H-1B drawing of lots in 2026? Nope. The H-1B draw of lots is randomly selected by USCIS in the spring of each year, and the new $4,000 rule is for approved H-1B.Extension phaseThe two are fully independent policies.

wandover-gbku4.title: CPT's abruptly suspended. International students like Princeton are restricted.
wandover-gbku4.dek: The Trump Government has tightened the CPT approvals, and schools named Princeton, NYU, UC Berkeley and others have been suspended from non-compulsory internships, and F-1 student out-of-school jobs have been significantly reduced.
wandover-gbku4.body:
Since August 2026, the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has issued new guidance to narrow the scope of CPT approval to a degree project where internships are necessary for graduation. CPT applications have been suspended or severely restricted successively by leading schools such as Princeton, NYU, UC Berkeley and the University of Washington, which means that the vast majority of F-1 students are largely blocked from completing their out-of-school internships through the CPT prior to graduation, and OPT ' s strategic planning has become more critical than ever.

---

Key points

  • ICE issued two memoranda on 12 August and 24 August 2026Schools are required to approve CPT only when internships are mandatory for degrees.
  • Princeton, NYU, UC Berkeley, Columbia University, Washington UniversityCPT approvals have been suspended or tightened, affecting institutions with the highest concentration of international students across the United States.
  • Most undergraduates and most studies Fan.Out-of-school internship authorization will no longer be available through the CPT and will be transferred to OPT.
  • The total duration of OPT is up to 12 months.(Totals before and after graduation), STEM may apply for an additional 24 months extension; when CPT is tightened, OPT-level protection becomes critical.
  • An early internalization, background upgrade and interview preparation are the most effective hedge strategies to get a formal offer during the OPT window.

---

What did the new CPT rule say? Which schools were affected?

According to the memoranda issued by the United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to schools on 12 August and 24 August 2026, ICE has enacted legislation in forceA stricter explanation.: CPT approval must correspond strictly to "an indispensable part of an established curriculum" and the internship must beCompulsory requirements for graduation, instead of taking credit.

The new regulations do not modify the lower federal statute itself, but the DHS explicitly warns that if the school approves the CPT for projects that do not require a traineeship, it will not be able to do so.Could result in the school losing its accreditation for international students.I don't know. This sit-in clause directly promotes quick follow-up by schools.

Main institutions in operation (as of September 2026):

SchoolMeasures
Princeton University1 September: CPT will no longer be approved for undergraduate students and most graduate students
New York University (NYU)Suspension of all pending and forthcoming CPT applications
UC BerkeleyComprehensive suspension of CPT approval
University of WashingtonSuspension of CPT approval
Columbia UniversityNot fully suspended, but tightened to the extent necessary for graduation
University of Illinois, Champagne BranchFollow-up review to limit mandatory CPT

Princeton is currently the only project that retains CPT eligibility.PSIA Master of Public AffairsandBendheim Master of Finance— Because internships in these two projects are a formal requirement for graduation.

---

After CPT tightens, does OPT work? What's the difference between OPT and CPT?

The CPT and OPT are the two main out-of-school work authorizations under the F-1 visa, with different positions and different policy pressures.

CPT vs OPT core comparison:

Relative dimensionsCPTOPT
Phase of applicationDuring readingUp to 90 days before or after graduation
Approving authorityInternational Students ' OfficeUSCIS (Federal application)
Total durationUnlimited (during reading)Up to 12 months
STEM ExtensionNot applicable+24 months (DHS Specialization)
Current policy risksNew rules have been tightened.Under pressure from the Trump government, but still available.
Difficulty of applicationRelatively simple (through schools)Direct submission to USCIS with longer processing cycles

Important logic: In the past, students have generally chosen to accumulate their work experience with CPT prior to graduation, thereby retaining the full 12-month OPT amount after graduation. Now that the CPT channel is blocked, a large number of students will start using OPT after graduation, which meansThe time pressure to get a full-time offer + H-1B drawing of lots within a limited period of 12 months is extremely high。

---

CPT's gone. What about a student internship? What are the viable paths?

This is at the heart of the search, which is currently the largest number of people. The reality is that the road has become narrower, but it has not been blocked.

Possible path combo:

  1. On-campus Employment
  • The F-1 visa allows work for up to 20 hours per week without additional authorization.
  • Princeton student Elizabeth Chen has made it clear that this option will be given priority.
  1. Post-Complement OPT
  • Up to 12 months after graduation, STEM may be extended to 36 months.
  • Key: The time to complete the job search during OPT + get an offer + finish the H-1B draw is very tight.
  1. School-funded internships
  • PICS in Princeton and RISENot affected by the new rules.As universities are directly involved in funding, they are not part of the CPT framework.
  • It is suggested that a query be made as to whether similar arrangements exist in schools.
  1. Remote/international internships
  • In theory, United States work authorizations are not required to work for companies outside the United States or for full teleworking. It is appropriate to build experience but not to build a local United States curriculum vitae.
  1. Pre-lock push and full-time opportunity.
  • This is the most strategic path:Access to interview process through internal push channels before OPT startsThe time of entry is aligned with the effective date of OPT.

Refpand data references: A significant proportion of the 300+ participants we mentored were internally pushed to Goldman Sachs, Meta, Amazon, TikTok and others offer during the CPT/OPT window. The essential advantage of introspection is that it skips the initial CV screening, which is the least friendly for international students. Our AI Agent reaches the 100+ company Hiring Team per week, with an average output of 5-15 effective introspections per week, which is particularly critical for the limited number of students in the OPT window.

My school hasn't been notified. Is my CPT still working? The new rules now require schools to comply with themselves, with different implementation tempo. Now that the CPT is tightened, the risk is naturally reduced, but the awareness of the OPT level remains important.

Are STEM students less affected? STEM students can still apply for an extension of OPT for 24 months after graduation (totalling 36 months), with a longer window period than STEM. However, CPT tightens up on all F-1 students, and STEM students have the same restricted access to internships.

Will the Trump government further restrict OPT? OPT is still protected by legislation, but political risks do exist. According to the public information available, OPT has not been abolished, but the pressure for new regulations continues. ai-anthropicopenai-0wane.dek: How difficult is OpenAI and Anthropic interviewing? From algorithms to AI ethics, the recruitment logic of the first line of AI is completely dismantled, and how to prepare students most efficiently.
ai-anthropicopenai-0wane.body:
In 2026, Anthropic and OpenAI became one of the world's most difficult employers of technology -- – Both companies have overvalued $100B, but recruitment is extremely limited and competition is far greater than FAANG. In order to get both of them, the depth of technology, the intellectual and cultural convergence, the pure paint of LeetCode is not enough.

Key points

  • It's a technical expedition.: Algorithms versus data structure against competitions (competition programming), while requiring ML theory + double-line fighting.
  • Ethical AI is a hard threshold.Anthropic and OpenAI both looked at AI safety, bias, social impacts during interviews, which is not sub-items, but baseline requirements.
  • Non-technical duty is equally high.: Posts such as PM, Research Ops, BD require a strong analytical capacity and a deep understanding of the AI industry.
  • High priority for operational experience: Experience in the use of PyTorch / TensorFlow, with LLM or large-scale distribution systems can significantly widen the gap.
  • Cultural and Mission AlignmentBoth companies place great emphasis on responsible AI development, and candidates who can clearly express their understanding of AI ' s mission in interviews are more popular.

---

What was the interview process for Anthropic and OpenAI?

The specific interview stages of both companies are confidential in-house, but the overall process is highly similar, depending on the industry discussions and open information, usually divided into the following rounds:

  1. CV screening/Recruiter Screen: Initial background screening, confirmation of match between basic technology warehouse and job.
  2. Technical Phone Interview1-2 rounds, calculator, data structure or ML base.
  3. Virtual Onsite: 4-6 consecutive rounds of interviews covering Coding, Systems Design, ML Design, Behavioral and Research Discussion.
  4. Bar Raiser / Culture Fit Round: Focus on understanding and teamwork.
Source: StartupHub.ai (Daniel Singer, 2026) indicates that the technical expeditions of these two companies, "frequently prepared to investigate complex problems", are among the recognized highest standards in the industry.

---

Technical interview? How?

Programming languagesPython (must), C++ (plus points)⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Preparatory policy

  • Algebra: at least 200+LeetCode Hard, with focus on Graph, DP, Sliding Windows, not just Mediam.
  • ML TheoryFrom the head, backpropagation, attestation mechanism, handwritten pseudocode is more important than back definition.
  • LLM ActualCandidates with model fine-twining, reasoning optimization or RAG project experience have a clear advantage in curricula vitae and interviews.
  • Distribution System: data parallelism vs. model parallelism, talking throughput bottleneck.

It is noteworthy that Anthropic is currently in the process of in-house testing of Claude Code's API service configuration (A/B test for optimising behaviour), which indicates that the company's understanding of system adaptability and AI behaviour is extremely demanding - interviews with candidates who can proactively talk about model service and best reason would be more impressive for interview officers.

---

What did Ethical AI say during the interview?

This is the link that many candidates from technical backgrounds are the easiest to ignore and the easiest to step on.

The core mission of Anthropic is to develop "reliable, interpretable, and capable Ai systems" and OpenAI is located in "building safe and secure, and intelligence". Both companies have written responsible AI into DNA, and it is almost impossible not to examine your ethical AI position in interviews.

Direction of common examination issues:

  • "What do you think AI's greatest social risk is, what would you do?"
  • "What would you do if you found out your training models were systematic?"
  • "What do you think of the al safety study?"

Response framework recommendations:

  1. Statement of position: Don't shy away, just tell me what you really think about AI safety.
  2. Specific examples: citation of real cases (e.g. the question of hallucination, the challenge of model alignment), not general.
  3. Combined posts: A description of how you're going to put your work in technical decision-making.

Among the trainees we mentored, the candidates who got the AI research lab offer, almost all showed real thinking about the AI safety, not recitation.

---

How do you prepare for this?

Anthropic and OpenAI also recruit a large number of unskilled posts, but the threshold is not below that of a technical post.

Non-technical core requirements:

  • Strong analytical capacity: to be able to drive decision-making with data, PM candidates need to demonstrate their perspective.
  • AI Industry Depth Understanding: Need for a real understanding of the LLM capability boundaries, the path to the landing of the AI product, rather than a superficial understanding.
  • Clear written and oral representationsResearch Ops and BD posts will focus on structured thinking and communication.
  • Strategic vision: to be able to discuss AI regulatory trends, competition patterns, commercialization pathways.

h1b-uscis-mcc7t.title: H1B's new grounds for revocation. Wage classification's fake. USCIS.
h1b-uscis-mcc7t.dek: USCIS found in Nebraska that IT had named the engineer "programmer" as a low-payer and directly cancelled H1B. This wave of law enforcement has to be seen by the students.
h1b-uscis-mcc7t.body:
In September 2026, USCIS discovered and cancelled a number of H1B petitions in Nebraska State - - It's not immigration, it's immigration.Irregular job classificationThe employer registers the actual employees working in the works as the lower-paid "computer programmer", which reduces the cost of wages. This law enforcement case marked the extension of the USCIS review of H1B from " whether or not to sign" to "the matching of job descriptions with actual jobs". In selecting H1B to sponsor employers, Chinese students must reassess the compliance risks of IT outsourcing companies.

---

Key points

  • USCIS voluntarily withdrew H1B petition in Nebraska, September 2026The reason was that the employer had violated salary compliance by misclassifying the engineer as a low-paid position (computer programmer).
  • Trigger mechanism is site visit + employee interviewUSCIS has worked with federal cooperation agencies to enforce the law.
  • Core Breach Logic: Employers reduce wage expenditure by lowering job classification, which constitutes “unfair competition” for local United States workers.
  • High-risk groupsH1B-sponsored holders obtained through the IT outsourced/human outsourcing company (body shop) are more likely to question the authenticity of the position.
  • If H1B is revoked, the holderCould lose legal status immediately.In particular, OPT-H1B students need to be registered in advance.

---

Why would USCIS cancel H1B? What's the irregularity?

H1B visa required the employer to submit it to USCISLabor Condition Application（LCA）It must state the job title, the SOC occupational code, and the correspondingPrevaling Wage。

The problem with the Nebraska case is:

  • EmployeesIt's actually an engineer-level job.(higher pay step)
  • But the petition for LCA and H1B is registered"computer programmer"(lower pay step)
  • As a result, employers pay less than what is required for a real job, in a disguised way saving the cost of working.
  • U.S.S. has determined that this constitutes an American worker working for H1B.Unfair wage competition
USCIS official statement: "We approved with federal partners to put an end to it and protect American workers from unfair wage and hiring practices."

This means,Even if the salary figures are higher than the Prevailing Wage on the LCA, there is a risk of being withdrawn as long as the job description does not correspond to the actual job.

---

What about USCIS?

USCIS.Site visits (ASVVP)This is the core tool for law enforcement. According to the information disclosed in this Nebraska case, the visitation process included:

Law enforcement stepsSpecific content
On-site raidsUSCIS officers travel to H1B holder ' s actual duty station to verify the work
Interviews with employeesDirectly ask the employee about his day-to-day duties, matching the LCA declaration of position
Federal law enforcementCross-checking of payroll records in collaboration with federal agencies such as DOL (Ministry of Labour)
The petition is withdrawn.USCIS withdrew H1B petition directly upon discovery of non-conformity

What kind of company is the easiest to find?

  • IT staffing / body shop (outsourcing to third-party clients)
  • Companies where the actual employee ' s place of work does not correspond to the place of registration of the LCA
  • An employer with a history of LCA irregularities.
  • Small companies that hand over H1B on a large scale but of a size that does not match business volume

---

What type of H1B holder is most at risk? How do you check for students?

Not all H1B holders are at equal risk. The following is a risk layer reference:

Type of employerRisk levelReason
Large direct employers of technology (Google, Amazon, Meta, etc.)LowTransparent internal pay system, job description compliance
Direct employers of financial institutions (Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, etc.)LowLCA is highly consistent with actual duties
Medium Technology/Consultancy (Deloitte, KPMG, etc.)MediumMulti-project site compliance
IT outsourcing/staffing agencyHighFuzzy job classification, assignment to client sites, wages below industry level
Small IT outsourcing (number of people)It's very high.Insufficient resources for compliance and high rate of historical violations

The self-check list (OPT → H1B conversion period) is particularly important:

  1. Confirm the SOC code on the LCA.Is it consistent with what you actually do (available at HR)
  2. VerificationWage: Login DOL FLC Data Center Querying the standard salary for the corresponding post
  3. Confirm.Actual duty stationCoverage at LCA registration Internal
  4. If you get H1B through staffing agency, confirmEnd client informationIs it filed in USCIS?
  5. Maintain all payroll, offer letter, job description documents as evidence of compliance

---

Common problems

Do I have legal status after H1B's withdrawn? Once the H1B petition has been withdrawn by the USCIS, the holder ' s H1B status is usually invalidated and, in the absence of other legal status (e.g. OPT, spouse H4, etc.), it is theoretically necessary to immediately stop work and initiate an identity remedy procedure; it is recommended that immigration lawyers be consulted first.

It was the employer ' s responsibility to disallow the wage classification. Why would my H1B be withdrawn? The subject of the H1B petition was the employer, but the holder was directly affected by the withdrawal. The withdrawal of the petition by USCIS does not amount to individual liability of the employee, but the holder loses his or her work status and therefore chooses to protect himself or herself in essence.

How do I know my employer doesn't have a LCA violation record? It can be done at the U.S. Department of Labor. LCA Disclosure Data The database provides public access to employer history LCA declarations, including payroll and past irregularities.

Isn't the H1B from the IT outsourcing company completely unable? Not absolutely unacceptable, but due diligence is required to confirm the size of the company, its historical compliance record, the transparency of the LCA and whether the final customer is a well-known enterprise. Risks are manageable, but the cost is higher than the direct employer.

Does USCIS sit witness give notice? USCIS site visits according to the ASVVP project rulesNo advance notice.In the case of surprise checks, employees need to be able to present their actual job responsibilities on the spot.

---

ai-22-25-16-qjtds.title: Stanford data: AI high-exposure jobs, unemployment rate rising to 16 per cent between the ages of 22 and 25
ai-22-25-16-qjtds.dek: Stanford research: How do students choose the direction of AI ' s high-exposure position, with 16 per cent unemployment rate between the ages of 22 and 25, and entry-level positions disappearing?
ai-22-25-16-qjtds.body:
The digital economy laboratory at Stanford University analysed over 25 million United States payroll data and found that:In high-visibility positions in AI, the number of workers aged 22-25 fell by 16 per cent between October 2022 and September 2025In contrast, the employment of workers aged 35-49 in the same job has increased by more than 8 per cent. This is not cyclical fluctuations, but rather a structural change that is reshaping the entry-level workplace – for North American Chinese students who are in the job-seeking window, the choice of the track is more important than the hard work of throwing their resumes.

---

Key points

  • Stanford Digital Economics LaboratoryAnalysis of 25 million + United States workers, employment rate in high-exposure positions 22-25 years16% Down(October 2022-September 2025).
  • Employment of workers aged 35-49Over 8% inverse; in the low exposure industry in AI, no age differentiation occurs.
  • In July 2026, Nolan Lovett, a researcher at NATO Special Operations University, published a paper in the peer-reviewed journal Human Resources Development Review, which for the first time named the phenomenon "Cognitive communal tragedy."。
  • What AI can do instead isProcessive cognitive tasks(data collection, formatting, first draft generation)Substantive validation judgement(judgement is right about this customer/ this market is right.)
  • The job-seeking strategy for students needs to be geared towards the functions of "AI difficult to independently validate": strategic judgement, cross-border collaboration, and high-risk decision-making.

---

What does Stanford's 16% data specify?

On 26 July 2026, Nolan Lovett published a peer review paper in Human Resources Development Review, citingStanford Digital Economics Laboratory(Stanford Digital Economic Lab) Labour market research led by Erik Brynjolfsson, Bharat Chandar and Ruyu Chen.

The core data are as follows:

IndicatorsValueData sources
The study covered United States wage earners.25 million+Stanford Digital Economics Laboratory
Statistical intervalOctober 2022-September 2025Ibid.
High exposure positions in AI, change in employment between 22 and 25 years of age−16%Brynjolfsson et al. 2026
High exposure positions in AI, change in employment between 35 and 49 years of age+ 8% or moreIbid.
Age differentiation of low-exposure positions in AINotIbid.
LinkedIn file sample analysis58 million copiesNBER, Hampole et al.

The independent analysis of 58 million LinkedIn files by NBER (National Bureau of Economic Research of the United States) reached similar conclusions: This pattern is more likeSystematic removal of developmental positions, not the average economic down cycle.

---

What do you mean, "cognito tragedy"? Why is the disappearance of entry-level posts a greater crisis?

In its paper, Lovett used the ecology concept of "the tragedy of the common land" to describe this mechanism.

Core logic:

  • At the corporate level: Replace primary cognitive tasks with AI, with immediate cost reductions and immediate efficiency gains — rational choice.
  • At the industry level: The junior position is the only soil to develop a "senior expert who can identify AI's mistakes". When a junior job disappears, in 10 years the whole industry will lack the capacity to do it.Substantive validationPeople.
  • Paradox: The cost of training now saved will be doubled in the future in the form of "no one can monitor AI output".

Lovett divides professional skills into two categories:

  • Internalized Mastery: The technically correct answer to the field of judgement accumulated through years of hard practice — doctors, lawyers, strategists — is the wrong answer to this case.
  • Distributional mastery: The ability to direct AI, review outputs and consolidate outputs - can be relatively quickly learned.

At the heart of the problem isValidation anchor"（Validation Tether）：

Distributional mastery cannot independently complete the substantive validation — the latter requires knowledge in the internalized field that has been removed from the culture pipeline by the AI induction wave.

A multi-centre study published in The Lancet Gastroenterology and Hepatology, led by Kasper Budzyryry, provides evidence of the physiological aspects: an amplifier who has been using AI-aided testing of saliva for a long time, after removing AI-aided patients, has been able to make a difference.Independent testing is below their own benchmark. LineI don't know. Skill degradation, real.

---

In 2026, which positions and tracks should North American students avoid?

This set of data is of direct reference value to Chinese students who are in the OPT/H1B job search window.

High AI exposure, high alternative risk function (requires caution or upwards):

  • Pure data entry/ report production (highly automated)
  • Standardized writing, first draft generation type writing
  • Ruled primary data extraction and visualization
  • Template financial modelling (base Excel level)

It is difficult for AI to completely replace and have a functional orientation against substitution:

  • Strategic judgement and operational understanding"Does this analysis make sense to the industry?"
  • Cross-border coordination and stakeholder managementProject management, consulting, client communication
  • High-risk decision-making situations: investment decision-making, legal judgement, medical diagnosis — AI can assist and humans have to sign
  • Creative origin and cultural context: Content strategies that require real human experience and insight
  • Development and governance of AI system itself:SE / ML Engineering / AI Security

Rexpand recommends a functional framework for student retention (2026):

Assessment dimensionsLow-risk track characteristicsHigh-risk track characteristics

Verify SubjectMankind must finally take responsibility.AI output delivered directly

Of the 300+ trainees we mentored, those who clearly identified "substantial judgment" candidates at the application stage-- – Whether it is possible to explain the reasonableness of the assumptions in an investment bank model or to design an experimental programme independently in a data science project – it is better to get an offer than a candidate who only demonstrates the use of tools.

---

Common problems

Does AI make it harder for students to find an OPT? Yeah, it's gonna be more competitive in AI's exposed primary functions. Data for the period 2022-2025 show a 16 per cent decline in employment in exposed positions in AI between the ages of 22 and 25, and OPT candidates are in the same age group and the choice of functional orientation is more critical than ever.

Which professions are the most affected? Functional shocks such as marketing, basic data analysis and standardized content production are most direct. CS / SDE as a whole still has a comparative advantage, but there are pressures on purely primary CRD development posts; quantitative finance, advisory strategy, AI project orientations are opposed to substitution.

"16% unemployment" means being laid off or not getting a job? The original study, which counted net changes in employment numbers, included a combination of reduced recruitment and lay-offs, and was not simply a concept of unemployment, but in the same direction: young workers in high-visibility positions in AI were systematically excluded from the labour market.

Does this study have an impact on the H1B drawing of lots? Indirectly. If AI continues to reduce the demand for primary jobs, the number and type of H1B-funded enterprises may shrink, and the sooner differential competitiveness (intropolation, professional background, judgement validation) is established, the more likely it is to get sponsored offer.

What help does Rexpand provide to cope with this trend? uber-3300-ai-b4i99.dek: Uber cut off 10 per cent of the staff, focused on management, and the analyst called "First victims of the AI era". What does it mean for North America to find a student?
uber-3300-ai-b4i99.body:
In 2026, Uber announced about 3,000 staff reductions, representing 10 per cent of its global workforce, representing the largest drawdown since the outbreak. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi made it clear that the goal was "to create a leaner, less hierarchical organization." This is a clear signal for North American Chinese students who are seeking employment: recruitment windows for large technology plants are tightening and competition is increasing further.

---

Key points

  • Size of staff reductionsUber reduced its workforce by about 3,000 employees, or 10 per cent of the total, to be the largest post-incident reduction in the company.
  • Focus on middle managementThis round of staff reductions concentrates on cutting down management levels and dismantling micro-teams of only one or two people.
  • Industry trend signalsAccording to Bob Sutton, a psychologist of the Stanford organization, this is a microcosm of the trend towards "simplified + expanded management" in science and technology enterprises.
  • Direct impact of student retention: The tightening of the HC (headcount) plant means that OPT/H1B is more competitive and the value of internal push channels is further highlighted.
  • Passiveness is no longer enough.: BCG Managing Director Julia Dhar warns that, without a reorganization of the accompanying process, the costs will rebound in the form of contractors/new offers — students will be able to take advantage of these “supplementation” opportunities.

---

Who is Uber? Why is middle management first?

Based on a letter from Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi to the full staff, the objectives of the reorganization are clear:

  • Reduction of management level（fewer layers of management）
  • Expansion of the management of existing managers（broader scope for remaining managers）
  • Dismantling a small team of 1-2 people（micro-teams）

Professor Emeritus at the University of Stanford, organizational psychologist Bob Sutton, divides the occupational groups into two categories: "grease people" (Lubricers, driving things to the ground) and "gunk people" (obstructors, consuming resources for power). He said that the wrong mid-level manager would "block the process, internalize the power", but that the middle-level was simultaneously carrying out a lot of "hidden work" — for example, coordinating the transfer of the department and finding out who would move things forward.

"Like making sure the handoffs work. Actually knowing who to go to gossip to get things done." — Bob Sutton, Stanford Professor Emeritus

Gallup's study of the United States workplace shows that the current average team size is12 personsThis represents an increase of about 50 per cent over 2013. Sutton was also a reminder that a team oversized by the General Assembly overstretched managers and instead became a decision-making bottleneck.

Source: Gallop U.S. Workplace Review (quoted by Bob Sutton)

---

Are we really saving money on layoffs? What did BCG experts say?

BCG Managing Director Julia Dhar spilled a cold water when interviewed:The scaling down does not necessarily save money in the long run.

Her logic is:

  1. Retrenchment is a temporary cost restructuring in the cost base.
  2. If we don't synchronize the workflow, the invisible workload will be reduced.Contractors or new recruitsForm back.
  3. Middle managers are less and less willing to do it -- they're the source of tomorrow's leaders.

Dhar also pointed out that, in the trend towards organizational flattening, decision-making would instead focus upwards — “not on the front line, but on the CEO” — contrary to the original purpose of the lay-offs.

Meaningful for students: When HC HC is tightened, it tends to shift to filling vacant posts. OPT holders with a technical background who have internal endorsements may be given the opportunity to do so during this "replacement" period.

  • Retrenchment of employees to the job market and increased supply of local candidates
  • H1B fixed (approximately 65,000 general quotas per year + 20,000 Master's quata) with increased competition intensity

Levels of remaining opportunity:

  • Enterprises use AI tools to improve efficiency and understand the increased demand for AI workforce candidates
