Common problems

What are the positions affected by Uber's downsizing? According to an open letter from the Uber CEO, this round of staff reductions focuses on the management level and the "one-two-person micro-team" aimed at streamlining the organizational structure and not on a single product line. The departments specifically affected are not fully open, but middle management functions bear the brunt.

Are there any opportunities to find a job during the OPTs when technology companies are cut off on a massive scale? Yes, but the strategy has to change. The HC freeze mainly affects ordinary delivery through the JD of the official network, while the internal channel is less affected — Hiring Manager has greater autonomy in recommending candidates. OPT job-seekers should give priority to the activation of the insider network rather than relying on seaboarding.

Will the H1B competition in 2026 be exacerbated by the loss of staff? Yeah. Empirical engineers have been laid off to return to the market and compete for the same positions as their current students, and these candidates usually do not need H1B sponsorship, putting direct pressure on students to stay in the market. It is crucial to get an offer as soon as possible and to find a company willing to sponsor.

Are middle management positions worthy of student retention? In the short term, there is a clear trend towards the compression of mid-level management in large plants, with a higher success rate of the target IC technology field (SDE/DA/DS/QI/FM). The mid-level management path is better suited for consideration after three to five years of experience.

Will the company be pushed after the layoffs? Yes, but a distinction needs to be made. Inward authority for staff members who have been laid off usually lapses immediately upon separation from service; however, active staff members can do so before separation, even if they are under pressure to retrench. It was important to establish relationships in advance and not to wait until the announcement.

wandover-vnxns.title: The Green Card? Career choices directly determine your migration prospects.
wandover-vnxns.dek: According to the latest report, the Indian applicant EB-2 Green Card is expected to wait 179 years and the selection of a student for a career must include consideration of the Green Card.
wandover-vnxns.body:
The latest analysis in 2026 shows that the waiting time for green cards varies by occupational group and nationality background by dozens of times - the Indian applicant EB-2 can be scheduled for 179 years, while the Chinese applicant EB-2 is expected to wait about 25 years and EB-1 about 5 years. In the case of Chinese students who are seeking employment in North America, there is a need for Chinese students who are seeking employment in North America.Choose which industry, which kind of visa priority you want, and decide your immigration time. LineThis factor is no less important than short-term remuneration.

---

Key points

  • As at December 2025The total number of occupational migrants in the three categories of EB-1/EB-2/EB-3 reached approximately1.26 millionThis represents an increase of 20.6 per cent over April 2020 (source: National Foundation for American Policy, NFAP).
  • Claimants of Chinese nationalityAfter 2026Applications submitted, expected to wait: EB-1 for approximately five years, EB-2 for approximately 25 years and EB-3 for approximately 7 years.
  • Indian applicantsAfter 2026Applications submitted, expected to wait: EB-1 for approximately 4-5 years, EB-2 for approximately 179 years and EB-3 for approximately 38 years.
  • The root cause of the backlog lies in two system constraints: annual only140,000.Number of professional migrants (as set by Congress in 1990), and no more than the total per country7%.
  • In September 2026, Visa Bolletin showed that the final date of action for Chinese nationality EB-2 was1 September 2021EB-3 is1 January 2022EB-1 is1 July 2023。

---

2026 What is the waiting time for each nationality / green card for each category?

According to the analysis published by NFAP in 2026,Application submitted after 2026The expected waiting period (simulated only, excluding government hearings, with actual results varying depending on individual priority dates, future policies, etc.):

---

Why is the green card backlog getting worse?

The NFAP report states that the underlying causes of the backlog are:Two structural institutional limitations, not an individual application factor:

1. Only 140,000 places per year (since 1990 unchanged) The 140,000 places include the main applicants and their spouses and children, and the number actually allocated to each category is well below 140,000. The United States Congress has not adjusted this figure since it was set in 1990, while the demand for highly skilled foreign labour has increased significantly over the same period.

Single-country ceiling of 7 per cent Regardless of the number of applicants in a given country, each country receives no more than 7 per cent of the total number of professional immigration visas per fiscal year. India and China have a long-term "card" in this ceiling due to the large population base and the high demand for highly skilled migrants.

How fast is the backlog? NFAP in 2016: More than98,000Indian applicants (including family members) were approved in the EB-2 category, but only those who actually received the green card4,407A net increase of over 90,000 per year. A similar pattern has followed each year since then.

As of December 2025,About a million Indian nationals.Waiting for a green card for occupational migrants, representing approximately the total backlog of EB-1/EB-2/EB-379%Of these, EB-2 has approximately 731,566 and EB-3 has approximately 213,414.

---

How does career choice affect your green card timeline?

For Chinese students who are seeking employment, the core message of this report is:Your choice of industry and employer determines which category you can apply for the green card, and how long you wait.

The following dimensions deserve special consideration:

Essential difference between EB-1 vs EB-2 vs EB-3

  • EB-1(b) Outstanding talent, executives of transnational corporations, or distinguished professors/researchers;No labour certificate (PERM)The approval process is relatively fast and currently has the shortest schedule (approximately five years) for applicants of Chinese nationality.
  • EB-2Senior degree professionals or persons with special abilities; required PERM (except NEW); Chinese nationality is currently scheduled for approximately 25 years.
  • EB-3Technical worker or baccalaureate requires a post; PERM is required; Chinese nationality is about seven years.

Is EB-2 NW (exemption from national interest) worth considering? NIW allows applicants to apply for EB-2 on their own without an employer ' s guarantee, often in the fields of STEM research, medical, engineering, etc. For Chinese students with academic/research background, NSW can bypass the PERM process but is still subject to the same EB-2 schedule (the final date for action by Chinese nationality is 1 September 2021).

Can employers speed up this process? Some large employers (e.g. technology, finance companies) have the resources to help employees to submit I-140 as soon as possible, setting earlier priority dates.Early entry into service, early submission of I-140In the long run, this means substantial advantages.

The hidden migration costs of industry choices

  • Selection of large transnational corporations (finance, science and technology): more likely to be supported by applications from the EB-1 category or to move to EB-1 via L-1;
  • Selection of small and medium-sized start-up companies: usually only EB-2/EB-3 and limited resources for employer support;
  • Frequent jumps: may affect the continuity of I-140 and the PERM process needs to be restarted.

The Trump Government has continued to tighten legal immigration checks since 2025, including increasing the cost of applications and expanding the scope of material reviews, and the United States Department of State has confirmed that the rate of visa issuance has declined in some countries. In this context,As early as possible layout, lock priority datesThe importance of this is further highlighted.

---

Common problems

How long will it take for a Chinese student to apply for a green card? According to the report issued in 2026 by the NFAP, if an application is submitted after 2026, the estimated waiting period is EB-1 for about five years, EB-2 for about 25 years and EB-3 for about seven years. Actual time depends on individual priority dates, future policy changes and the availability of visas.

EB-1 and EB-2 are more realistic for students? The majority of eligible students are initially on the EB-2 path (through their employer, PERM or NIW), as EB-1 requires outstanding talent or executive status as a transnational corporation. However, when entering top-level STI/FICs and accumulating sufficient success, applying for EB-1 upgrades after 5-8 years is a common strategy and waiting time for Chinese nationality is shorter.

September 2026, Visa Bulletin, what does it mean to me? Visa Bulletin is published monthly by the United States Department of State, indicating the final date of action for each category and nationality. Your I-140 priority date must be earlier than that date in order to enter the final green card approval (I-485 or the Consular visa). Chinese nationality EB-2 is currently 1 September 2021 and EB-3 1 January 2022.

STEM Professional green card censorship? Yeah. The United States Department of State has characterized each visa decision as a "national security decision", with some STEM areas (especially semiconductor, AI, aerospace, etc.) having longer review cycles and a higher percentage of RFE (additional evidence requirements). The selection of an occupation requires simultaneous assessment of the industry ' s risk of being reviewed.

Will frequent job changes affect the green card process? It has an impact. If you change employers before I-140 approval, the new employer usually needs to restart the PERM process, you will lose the original priority date. If I-140 has been approved for 180 days, priority dates can be carried, in part, through Act AC21, subject to certain conditions, and it is recommended that immigrant lawyers be consulted before the jump.

h1b-9-15-30-g8mhp.title: H1B has changed! Old forms have been rejected directly since September 15th, and salaries have increased by 30%.
h1b-9-15-30-g8mhp.dek: The USCIS announced that new versions of forms I-539 and I-765 were to be launched on 15 September, with the old versions being rejected without exception, while the H1B minimum wage was to be increased by 30 per cent to be observed by students.
h1b-9-15-30-g8mhp.body:
From 15 September 2026, USCIS will reject the old versions Form I-539 and Form I-765, without any grace period. Whether the H-4 spouse applies for EAD, the student maintains his/her status or other non-immigrant visa holders, the application must be returned directly and without opportunity for redress on or after 15 September using a new form with the symbol "September 15, 2026".

---

Key points

  • Entry into force of the deadlineSince 15 September 2026, old versions I-539 (old version: August 28, 2024) and I-765 (old version: August 21, 2025) have been rejected.
  • No grace period: USCIS makes it clear that there is no additional allowance, that old forms are sent back and that no new version can be submitted later.
  • New forms cannot be used earlier: A new version of the form indicating "September 15, 2026" shall likewise not be submitted until 15 September.
  • H1B is barely affected.The extension of the status of H-1B employees is usually handled by the employer through Form I-129, and I-539/I-765 mainly affects the H-4 spouse, specific students and other non-immigrant visa holders.
  • The government will issue a sample in advance.USCIS undertakes to publish samples of new forms and instructions for filling out them prior to their entry into force, and applicants should check the version numbers in due time.gov.

---

Who are specifically covered by the updated form of 15 September 2026?

Not all H1B-related personnel need immediate action, but the key is what form you use and who you are.

Main affected groups:

  • H-4 Spouses/childrenUse of I-539 for extension or non-immigrant status; H-4 spouse applying for EAD use of I-765.
  • Student visa holders F-1/J-1I-765 (e.g. OPT/STEM OPT authorization application) is required for partial change of status or EAD application.
  • Other non-immigrant visa holdersAny person who requests an extension or change of identity through I-539 or an authorization to work through I-765 is affected.

Usually not affected by this update:

  • H-1B employee ' s personal status is extended. Form I-129 is submitted to the employer, without reference to I-539/I-765.
  • The personal work authorization of H-1B employees is directly based on H-1B approval and does not require I-765.
Identity categoryCommon TablesWhether or not affected by the 15 September update
H-1B staff (extension/change of identity)Form I-129 (submitted by employers)No impact.
H-4 Spouses/children (renewed status)Form I-539• Impact, new version required
H-4 Spouses (application for EAD)Form I-765• Impact, new version required
F-1 student (OPT/STEM OPT)Form I-765• Impact, new version required
Other non-immigrants (EAD application)Form I-765• Impact, new version required

---

How do the dates of the new and old versions differ? How do you confirm the correct form?

The USCIS table version number is printed at the bottom right or lower left corner of the table, usually in the form of "Edition Date" or a direct date.

Comparison of versions of tables:

TableOld version date (received after 15 September)Date of new edition (used on 15 September)
Form I-539August 28, 2024September 15, 2026
Form I-765August 21, 2025September 15, 2026

Operational step recommendations:

  1. Now.: Enter USCIS.gov The official network confirms the current downloadable version and its date on the corresponding table page.
  2. September 15th.: download and submit only versions indicating "September 15, 2026", not using any old local cache PDF.
  3. Advance preparation: If your EAD is due between September and October, it is recommended that the old version be submitted in time by 14 September, or that the new version be submitted after 15 September, so as to avoid the old and new alternation periods.
  4. Prohibition of advance submission of new editions: Not to submit a new version of the form by 15 September, which would similarly result in rejection.
Important Reminder: USCIS indicates that a new version of the forms will be available by 15 September, with instructions, and that it will be important to read the most up-to-date versions of the forms, as updates of the forms usually accompany minor changes in the filling requirements.

---

What does it mean to have no grace period? What happens if the application is rejected?

This is where vigilance is most needed for this update.USCIS expressly stated that there was no additional grace period (No Grace Perud).

Specific consequences:

  • Directly Revert: The old form was submitted on or after 15 September 2026 and the application will be returned and not processed.
  • Don't give me a chance.: Unlike in some cases when additional material can be provided by RFE (ReQuest for Employment), there is no opportunity for the wrong version of the table to be resubmitted ex post facto — a new version will have to be submitted again in its entirety.
  • Could lead to an empty window.For H-4 spouses or OPT students who are nearing the expiry of EAD and are in urgent need of renewal, the withdrawal may result in the interruption of work authorization and affect their working status.

Among the trainees we mentored, table type errors were often not due to the lack of deadlines, but to the use of expired PDF downloads from other sources. It is recommended that each submission be downloaded directly from the USCIS.gov official network and not dependent on third-party websites or historical archives.

---

Common problems

Do H1B work visa holders need a new version of I-539 or I-765? Not normally required. The extension of the identity of H-1B employees is submitted by the employer through Form I-129 and the work authorization is based directly on the approval of H-1B, without the need for I-765. This update mainly affects spouses of H-4 and some student visa holders.

Would it be acceptable to submit the old version of the form by 14 September? Yes. According to USCIS, old versions of the forms submitted by 15 September may still be accepted; the key point is 15 September, when the old versions are rejected on or after that date.

Can the new version of the form be downloaded and completed in advance and submitted on 15 September? A new version of the form could be downloaded and completed in advance, but not by 15 September. A new version of the form is equally invalid before the effective date.

Should H-4 EAD, which is due to expire, submit an extension by 15 September or later? If your materials are ready, it is recommended that the old version of I-765, which is currently in force, be submitted by 14 September, so that an empty identity window can be avoided while waiting for the new version. If it is too late, it will be submitted as soon as the new edition is downloaded on 15 September, with an automatic extension (if conditions are met).

Where can the new form of 15 September 2026 be downloaded? The only official channels are the Form I-539 and Form I-765 pages of the USCIS official website Uscis.gov. As of 15 September, the page will be updated as a download link to a new version, the date of which should be shown as "09/15/26".

cpt-f-1-uc-berkeley-qgur7.body:
On 27 August 2026, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) of the Government of Trump issued a memorandum to all U.S. higher education institutions to significantly tighten the qualifications of international students for the CPT (Curricular Practical Training) internships - only in the case of formal partnerships between employers and schools and compulsory curriculum requirementsAll studentsF-1 students are required to undergo practical training (including native American students) to attend internships. ---

What did the new rules change?

Previously, F-1 students had access to a student visa for summer internships or part-time internships, with a relatively flexible threshold, and many universities had a more liberal CPT approval process.

New requirements specified in the DHS Memorandum (applicable from August 2026)：

  1. Must exist between employer and schoolFormal cooperation agreements（formal agreement）。
  2. The internship is requiredAll studentsBoth (American citizens + international students) are involved in substantive work training and cannot be set up solely for international students.
  3. CPT Internships must be in the relevant degree programmeDirect component, instead of optional additional items.

In his press release, the DHS spokesman made it clear that "schools and employers should know that they have been warned. Under President Trump, the abuse of this generous system will no longer be tolerated."

---

Sandra Ding, a student of Chinese nationality attending Berkeley, said that Berkeley had been chosen between universities in Singapore, the United Kingdom and the United States, the core reason being career development opportunities — but in the current policy environment, she said that if she chose again, she would not choose to go to American universities. ai-sec-quant-gvl30.body:
In July 2026, the net monthly value of the AI hedge fund Situnational Awairness fell by 67 per cent and was then forced to sell most of the shares to Citadel under Ken Griffin's banner as "sell price". As of 24 August 2026, according to Bloomberg and Yahoo Finance, the SEC had issued summonses to four Wall Street banks in United States banks, Citi, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Chase to investigate the scale and timing of the Fund ' s lending. Key points

  • AUM was over $20 billion at the peak of the fund.In the first half of the year, the return was as high as 439 per cent, but the window was extremely narrow with high leverage.
  • It's not a stock error, it's a debt problem.: Borrowed money makes the increase look amazing, and the Fund loses its ability to wait when it reverses.
  • Core alerts for job seekers: Before entering the quant/AI hedge fund track, the risk management culture of the target company needs to be judged, not just AUM figures or salaries.

---

What is the full timeline for the Situal Awareness event?

General Awareness was created in 2024 by Leopold Aschenbrenner. Aschenbrenner, a former OpenAI researcher, was widely known in the AI community for his long article, “Situational Awareness”, the core argument of which is that the pace of progress in AI will go far beyond market expectations.

The question that this timeline reveals is not whether the AI theme is correct, but whether it is.The funds borrowed have deprived the Fund of its patience to wait for a return.I don't know. The long-term investment logic becomes a minor issue once the payment is demanded by the prime broker.

---

Why would the SEC investigate banks, not just the Fund itself?

The size and mechanisms of the Situal Awarenes are different, but the three elements of "concentrated hold + leveraged + bank horizons are clearer than external investors".

Note that:SEC subpoenas don't amount to charges.I don't know. Bloomberg cited the SEC spokesperson that investigations by regulatory bodies did not represent the funds or banks that had been the subject of investigations and might not end with enforcement actions. Neither the territorial Awairness nor the four banks were formally charged with any misconduct.

The incident exposed a structural vulnerability point of the ACSF and had a direct reference value for students who were seeking employment.

For North American Chinese students, entering the quant/AI hedge fund track is not unworthy — traditional institutions such as Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley and Citi remain well positioned in the field of quantification and AI investment and more mature compliance systems.The question is how to identify which types of companies are real opportunities and which are only leverage-driven short-term prosperity.

In the last week, the party agreed to do 1:1 and ask three questions:

Sent a precise letter of thanks (Say thank you-Specifically)

HC, Roffe reminds:Your supervisor might introduce you to the rest of their network.I don't know. "If you make a good impression, they really want to help you."

kpmg-500-qduzq.body:
KPMG officially launched the cost-cutting plan codenamed Project Victor in August 2026, with the first phase reducing about 24 partners and 450 employees to a total of about 500. For North American Chinese students who are sprinting on Big Four consultancy positions, this is a signal that needs to be confronted: the four major recruitment tempo and headcount planning is tightening, with early layout to avoid risk.

  • Background reasons: Cost-control superimposed with a document misuse scandal shock collection, KPMG simultaneously seeks financial support from global parent companies.
  • Impact of student retentionThe consultation sector has tightened, competition for H1B/OPT posts has intensified, and four strategic risks have increased.
  • Response direction: Fragmented objectives (financial, scientific and technical, advisory) + Internal push acceleration is the most effective defence strategy at present.

---

What is KPMG Project Victor? What's the size of the layoffs?

According to the Australian Financial Review (AFR) on 20 August 2026, Project Victor is a systematic cost reduction project initiated within KPMG, not a single small-scale adjustment.

Numbers known during phase I:

Affected groupsNumberTime nodes
PartnersSome 24 (additional)Signed by the Board in late August 2026
General staff (Staff)About 450Ibid., phase I
Total expected impactApproximately 500 personsSome partners leave after the end of the month bonus.

It's worth noting that some of the partners are waiting for the end of the fiscal year in August 2026 to be officially released... In other words,Actual separations are likely to be higher than the first-phase bulletin figures。

In addition, KPMG negotiated financial support simultaneously with global parent companies against the background of a "document abuse scandal" that had hit their revenues, suggesting that the layoffs were not simply efficiency optimizations, but rather passive contractions under external pressure.

---

Big Four, what is the practical impact of retrenchment on students seeking employment?

For Chinese students with OPT or ready to smoke H1B, four major changes in headcount directly affect offer. The following are some key linkages:

1. Possible concomitant reduction of recruitment quotas During layoffs, the four majors usually freeze or compress new headcount approvals simultaneously. Even if the official posts are still on the board, the actual open requisition may have been stopped internally.

2. H1B precautionary rise The consulting firm had been cautious about the drawing of lots for H1B and, under pressure of staff reductions, had preferred to recruit candidates who did not need a sponsorship.

3. Inverse spillovers of competitors The dismissed KPMG employees will be in the same job market (Deloitte, PwC, EY, consulting firms) and the pool of competitors facing students will be expanded directly.

4. Reduction of time windows If your OPT expires before the end of 2026, now the window is pretty tight to get the offer and complete the entry process.

---

What should we do now? Three implementable strategies

It is the most dangerous practice to wait blindly for four major openings or only to consult in the face of the tightening of the consultation tracks. Following are some of the directions that we have repeatedly tested in coaching our students:

Strategy One: Multiple Targets, Non-Custodial Counselling

Consulting, Finance and Tech are parallel lines and mutually reinforcing. Among our mentors, many of the four originally targeted consultations ended up in Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Capital One, Deloitte, and so on.

Strategy II: Inner push takes precedence over sea landing

In a tight climate of headcount, the rate of internal push is much higher than the rate of Internet conversion. Inner LinkedIn in Rexpand Agent actively touches 100+ Hiring Team per week, producing 5-15 introspective opportunities for participants; email is attached to a 1 million+ mail repository, with a response rate of about 20%.

Strategy III: Filling the curriculum vitae gap with background promotion projects White

Each direction will be closed by referral, with a working mentor, 1v1, who can write directly into the curriculum vitae.

According to the AFR report of 20 August 2026, no specific departments are currently disclosed, with only the first phase being confirmed to involve some 24 partners and 450 employees. The scope of the additional post reductions has yet to be made public upon the formal signature of the KPMG Board of Directors.

Does KPMG still offer students H1B sponsorship? The official KPMG has not yet announced the cancellation of the H1B policy, but there has been a general tightening of the processing of the sponsorship applications during the layoffs. It is suggested that when applying, recruiter is asked about the current sponsorship status and is synchronised to prepare an alternative offer that does not depend on sponsorship.

Big Four Retrenchment, Deloitte / PwC / EY? There is currently no public information indicating that the other three have similar plans, but the consulting industry as a whole faces macro-pressures and recommends that sustained attention be paid to official announcements and not to rely on single companies as sole targets.

During OPT, there was a layoff at the target company. Yes, but pay attention to the maximum number of days OPT unemployed (STEM OPT is 90 days). It is recommended that multi-line applications be launched as soon as possible, without waiting for a complete failure in one direction, otherwise the time window would be very passive.

Is it worth the student consultation now? Worth it, but the strategy has to be adjusted. The four main groups remain important employers, the key being: one with strong internal push channels; two with project-supported curricula vitae; and three without a single bet on one or another industry.

42-h1b-vi1qw.title: American international students are down by 42,000! Texas is driving out H1B. What do we do with students?
42-h1b-vi1qw.dek: DHS latest data: in August, 42,000 students were cut back to their nine-year-old level in the United States; the Governor of Texas threatened the public school system "Zero H1B". Double space, signal clear.
42-h1b-vi1qw.body:
In August 2026, US DHS' latest SEVIS data showed that the number of international students in school dropped by about 42,000 a month, from about 1.15 million to about 1.11 million a month, returning to their nine-year-old level; at the same time, the Governor of Texas, Greg Abbott, publicly stated that he was going to achieve "exactly zero" foreign employees in the public school system, completely blocking the use of H1B. The combination of two policy signals is a serious warning to Chinese students seeking employment in the United States.

---

Key points

  • Single month - 3.7 per centIn July-August 2026, SEVIS active student records decreased from about 1.15 million to about 1.11 million, a reduction of about 42,000 (source: DHS SEVIS Data Mapping Tool).
  • The largest decrease in student retention in ChinaIn August, China recorded an active record of 197,802, a decrease of 6,666 compared to July, the highest absolute monthly decline in all countries.
  • New threat to H1B, Texas.: Governor Abbott claims that H1B employees will be banned from the public school system, targeting "exactly zero" foreign employees, covering a wide range of positions such as teachers, administration, etc.
  • Systemic deterioration of the policy environmentAccording to immigration lawyers, the decline in SEVIS is not just seasonal fluctuations, but is a structural signal of the decline in the attractiveness of the United States to international talent.
  • Increased competition for private jobs: When the public/education sector narrows down, there will be an increase in the number of job-seekers in private business tracks, such as finance, technology and so forth, and the importance of contextual differences and inward promotion resources will increase.

---

In August 2026, international students dropped by 42,000: what is behind the numbers?

According to the DHS data mapping tool for SEVIS (Student and Exchange Vision Information System), U.S. Active International Student Record in August 20261,110,000 peopleDecrease from approximately 1,150,000 in July About42,000Month drop3.7%I don't know. This figure tracks the F-1 academic visa and related non-immigrant categories, excluding dependent visa holders.

Monthly comparison of major source country movements (July-August 2026)：

Chinese students need special attention.China is the country with the largest absolute decline in a single month (-6,666), while India ' s absolute decline is even smaller, despite its larger total. This trend is directly related to the tightening of visa reviews in recent years and the increase in uncertainty in SEVIS records.

It is worth noting that the termination of SEVIS records does not always amount to expulsion or the cancellation of visas — graduation, transfer and completion of projects trigger termination. But the immigration lawyer Keshab Raj Seadie made it clear that the recent decline "is not to be seen as merely seasonal fluctuations" but "the United States is becoming more difficult and less attractive to international students."

---

Texas H1B ban: What is the substantive impact on the job search of students?

The Governor of Texas, Greg Abbott, has recently publicly announced plans to ban the use of H1B visas in the public school system, with the goal of achieving "exactly zero" for foreign employees. This statement covers teachers, administrative and other public education positions.

Can not open message：

  • Scope of impactThe current focus on the K-12 public school system does not directly restrict private enterprises and university scientific posts.
  • Legal levelH1B is a federal visa, and the possibility of direct legislative restrictions by state governments remains controversial; however, even at the legal level, policy signals have actually deterred employers.
  • Indirect impact on finding employment for studentsThe public/educational sector is restricted, which means that H1B posts could have been provided to students, and that the competitive pressure of job-seekers on private financial, technological and technological enterprises will be more concentrated.

Which jobs are relatively safe (private)：

Industry orientationRepresentative company (example track)H1B Sponsorship History
Technology/SWEGoogle、Meta、Amazon、AppleHistory is stable.
Finance/IBGoldman Sachs、J.P. Morgan、Morgan StanleyStabilization
Financial technologyStripe、Capital OneStabilization
ConsultantsBCG、Deloitte、KPMGMore stable
Public K-12 education (Tex)—High risk. Policy tightening.

---

What if the SEVIS records were terminated during OPT?

The termination of SEVIS records is one of the most worrying risks for international students today. Once the records have been terminated, the student ' s immigration status ceases to be active and normally cannot continue to study or legally work in the United States unless the records are restored or the student completes the change of status.

Common causes of termination of SEVIS (not all enforcement operations)：

  • Normal graduation, end of course.
  • Transfer or transfer
  • Authorized absences/dismissals
  • Volume data changes resulting from policy adjustments (partial recovery after mass termination in 2025)
  • Real visa violations or enforcement actions

Recommendation of immediate steps if SEVIS records are terminated：

  1. Contact DSO.This was confirmed as a result of systemic changes or individual irregularities.
  2. Advice to licensed immigrant lawyers, assess the feasibility of recovery.
  3. Don't leave without permission.The departure may trigger additional restrictions.
  4. Check OPT/STEM OPT authorization status, to confirm that the validity of EAD is not affected by SEVIS status.

Among the trainees we mentored, there were people who were able to obtain interviews at the first opportunity after the restoration of their status during the SEVIS temporary anomaly due to the advance internalization of the channels, even if the process was delayed — time difference management was critical.

---

In the context of deteriorating policies, what should be done to adjust the job-seeking strategy for students?

A tight policy environment does not mean that opportunities disappear, but it does mean thatThe wrong space is smaller, the window is shorter.。

Core strategy adjustments in the current environment：

  • Preferably locking down private companies willing to sponsor.Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Meta, Google, Stripe, among others, have recorded the stabilization of H1B sponsorship as a top priority in their history.
  • Inner Push>Introduction: SEVIS uncertainty makes many HR more cautious about international students; insider candidates can bypass the hidden barriers of initial screening and enter the hiring manager horizon.
  • Accelerate background differentiation: DA/DS/QI/FM/SE has a project conclusion +referral background that is more compelling than mere resume in the context of tight policies and the influx of competitors into private enterprise tracks.
  • Shortening the job search cycle(b) Get an offer before OPT starts, as far as possible, to avoid being exposed to SEVIS risks during the period of unemployment.

The AI Agent (Claude Drive) of Rexpand covers 100+ Hiring Team per week, producing 5-15 real introspectives; our 1,000+ serving mentors (on average, over 5 years, covering 200+ companies) can directly help the participants bypass the cold hole.

---

Common problems

Does the H1B ban in Texas affect international student employment in the United States? Students who need to continue their studies, complete their OPT or STEM OPT must submit their request for Extension of State (EOS) to USCIS, or face the risk of illegal stay.   • There's a transition arrangement for American students.: F-1 students who have entered the country before 2026-09-15 can stay until the end of Program End Date or OPT/STEM OPT on I-20, but must not exceed2030-11-14。
  • OPT/STEM OPT must apply for EOS separatelyAdditional time is required to complete OPT or STEM OPT, and an EOS application must be submitted to USCIS, not automatically.
  • Form I-539 is core material: EOS Application Core Form, USCIS must receive before "Admit Until Date" expires.
  • You can apply for EOS 180 days in advance.: Do not wait until the last minute, late application or omission will have a direct impact on the legitimacy of identity.

sevp-cpt-day-1-cpt-5r0yl.title: SEVP suddenly went after CPT!
sevp-cpt-day-1-cpt-5r0yl.dek: On August 12, 2026, SEVP issued a CPT warning to the National University of Higher Education that UC Berkeley, UCSD had been suspended on that day and Day 1 CPT had ushered in the most critical period of review.
sevp-cpt-day-1-cpt-5r0yl.body:
On August 12, 2026, SEVP (American Student and Exchange Visitors Project) issued a broadcast notice to all DSOs in the United States of America, BCM2608-01, warning severely of CPT abuse -The CPT wasn't completely cancelled, but the era of "work visas with CPT" was over.I don't know. UC Berkeley immediately suspended the Course Credit CPT on the same day, after which UC San Diego temporarily suspended all F-1 CPT applications. If you're practicing with CPT, or you're going to follow Day 1 CPT, this article is the information you need most at this time.

---

Key points

  • SEVP issued BCM2608-01 on 12 August 2026With immediate effect, the National School DSO is required to scrutinize whether the CPT mandate is "essential" to the curriculum.
  • The CPT itself was not cancelled.But there has been a fundamental shift in auditing logic: from "professionally relevant" to "degrees necessary and all students must complete".
  • UC Berkeley suspends Course Credit CPT, UCSD temporarily suspends all CPT applicationsMore schools are expected to follow suit.
  • Day 1 CPT is the focus of the reviewIf it cannot be proved that CPT is part of the course "integral", it may be considered unauthorized work, affecting F-1 status and future immigration records.
  • DSO has signed I-20 authorizing CPT to be tantamount to "a sworn testimony", and violation of the authorization may result in schools being revoked from SEVP accreditation and facing HSI fraud investigation.

---

What exactly did SEVP BCM2608-01 warn?

On 12 August 2026, SEVP (under ICE) sent a broadcast message BCM2608-01 to the designated school officer (DSO) of the National School of America. It's not congressional legislation, it's not an official USCIS regulation, but...SEVP administrative warning and compliance guidelines for schoolsBut the effect is immediate — effective on the day of publication.

The core allegations of the circular are that SEVP found "an increase in the number of non-compliant CPT authorizations", that a large number of approved CPT jobs in schools are not really closely related to the students' established curriculum (curriculum), and that some schools actually operate with CPT as a disguised work permit.

SEVP makes three specific requests for DSO:

  1. Individual reviewsExisting CPT applications to verify whether the work content matches the requirements of the professional course.
  2. Only when a training is required to complete a degree, and all students in the profession are required to complete a degree- to approve the CPT.
  3. Sufficient documentation must be retained.Proof of "course necessity"; voluntary consultation with SEVP in case of uncertainty.

These three requirements directly block past CPT operations.

---

Did the CPT get canceled? Why did UC Berkeley and UCSD pause?

CPT was not cancelled nationwide. However, the emergency actions of the two UC universities released strong policy tightening signals.

SchoolActionsTime of entry into forceType of impact
UC BerkeleyCourse Credit CPTEffective 12 August 2026Course crediting CPT
UC BerkeleyKeepRegular processing, approximately 5 working daysCPT Essential Degrees
UC San Diego (ISEO)Temporary suspension of all F-1 CPT applicationsSince 12 August 2026All CPT types
UCSD DescriptionRecovery pending further guidance from SEVPTo be determined—

The UC Berkeley treatment revealed a clear dividing line:Degree-required CPT (specified requirements for degree) vs. Course Credit CPTI don't know. The former can still apply normally, while the latter is suspended immediately.

The wording of the UCSD statement is even more noteworthy: "F-1 CPT remains an optional path, but ISEO is temporarily suspending the processing of applications pending further guidance on the CPT issuance policy update. This means that the UCSD has been proactive in setting off brakes after the policy has been updated, rather than declaring the CPT permanently terminated.

The precise judgement is that:The CPT system still exists, but the auditing logic is being rewritten and schools are already protecting themselves in advance.

---

Day 1 CPT can still go? What are the risks to the F-1 identity?

Day 1 CPT, i.e. students working full-time through the CPT as soon as they enter school, is the central target of this BCM 2608-01.

Why is Day 1 CPT the highest risk:

  • Day 1 CPT projects are usually based on "quick access to work permits" rather than on strict curriculum necessity.
  • The new requirements of SEVP are clear: CPT must be "all students in this profession are required to complete" - most Day 1 CPT projects cannot meet this standard.
  • SEVP made it clear.Check and request DSO to provide proof at any time.The CPT that was approved in the past could have been turned over.

Specific consequences of non-compliance of CPT for F-1 students:

  • "unauthorized employment"
  • Legitimacy that directly affects the status of F-1 students
  • Permanent retention in immigration records affecting future H-1B, green card applications, etc.
  • As a result, schools may be revoked and students forced to transfer or leave the country

Consequences for schools:

  • DSO signed CPT authorizing I-20 to be tantamount to "under oath of testimony" and, if SEVP found a violation, DSO individuals faced legal consequences.
  • Serious circumstances may lead to the withdrawal of the school ' s SEVP accreditation and the loss of eligibility for F-1/M-1 students.
  • The involvement of the Homeland Security Investigation (HSI) in fraud investigations could be triggered.

What needs to be specifically stated isThe CPT warning and the D/S rule, which came into effect in the first half of 2026, are two separate matters: The D/S rules affect the length of time I-94 and OPT, while BCM 2608-01 is a specific enforcement notice at the level of CPT compliance, without confusion.

---

What should we do now that we are using or planning to apply?

Do not panic, but must verify their situation immediately. The following is a list of our proposed actions:

If you're already practicing with CPT:

  • Contact your DSO to confirm whether your CPT mandate corresponds to the course 'Degree-required', not just the grades.
  • Do not change employer, job content or workplace without permission- CPT mandates are tied to specific employers, courses and time nodes, and any changes require prior reauthorization.
  • Maintain all CPT-related curriculum materials, offer letter, job description documents for school or SEVP review.

If you're going to apply for CPT:

  • Psychological preparation for more material than in the past and longer time for approval — the risk of compliance by DSO increases and the audit scale is bound to tighten.
  • Ask DSO in advance whether your project belongs to the Degree-required CPT and whether it can be certified in writing.
  • If you are currently in the Day 1 CPT project, it is recommended that one-on-one communication with the consultant or the DSO be made as soon as possible to assess whether the project can withstand the SEVP review.

Long-term identity planning:

  • CPT should not be used as a "stand-by" for H-1B or as a solution for long-term identity. The SEVP circular clearly points to the operating models of "maintenance through continuous reading".
  • Formal CPT + OPT + H-1B routing must be based on real curriculum needs and work experience, rather than on policy gaps.

---

Common problems

Is the CPT completely canceled? Nothing. SEVP ' s BCM2608-01 is not a cancellation order, and the legal internship system for CPT as an F-1 student still exists. The real hit was the operating model of "the use of CPT as a disguised work permit", especially the Day 1 CPT type project.

UC Berkeley and UCSD suspend CPT. Can I apply? Depends on your school and CPT type. The UC Berkeley still accepts the Degree-required CPT application (approximately five working days); the UCSD is currently temporarily suspending all CPT applications pending further guidance from SEVP. It is recommended to contact directly the DSO at your school to confirm the latest status.

Will the CPT I'm using be traced? SEVP explicitly has the right to randomly check and request from DSO supporting documentation, including approved CPT authorization records. If your CPT is approved through Day 1 CPT school or a less relevant project, it is recommended that compliance risks be assessed as soon as possible.

Is BCM 2608-01 and D/S the same thing? Nope. The D/S Rules (Duration of Status) are the official regulations in force in the first half of 2026, the I-94 period of stay and OPT calculations affecting F-1 students; and the BCM2608-01 is a special administrative issuance for CPT compliance, which are independent and not confused.

If my CPT were found to be non-compliant, would it affect H-1B or green card applications? Yes. Non-compliant CPTs may be identified as "unauthorized work", a record that will remain permanently in the immigration file, with potentially negative implications for future H-1B drawings and green card approvals.

---

oracle-21000-opt-av89q.dek: Oracle has downsized 21,000 people, with an additional double-digit percentage cut by September. Where are the mined areas where students are left to find work?
oracle-21000-opt-av89q.body:
Oracle has reduced its staff by approximately 21,000 (a 13 per cent reduction) in the FY2026 fiscal year as of May 2026, and a new round of double-digit percentage reductions is now planned for some teams by 1 September 2026. For North American Chinese students who were holding H1B or who were still studying at OPT, this round of layoffs is not just a problem for Oracle - It reflects the structural contradiction between the input of the entire large technology plant in AI and the pressure for profit, directly affecting the recruitment budget and the willingness to sponsor visas.

---

Key points

  • Oracle FY2026 has down 21,000.This represents 13% of the total number of employees and currently approximately 141,000 (source: Oracle regulatory documents).
  • The new retrenchment target is completed by 1 September.Some of the team cuts may be double-digit (source: Business Insider, 11 August 2026).
  • AI infrastructure is the main cause.: Oracle FY2026 infrastructure expenditure amounted to $55.7 billion, exceeding the cash flow of $23.7 billion for the year, filling the gap by borrowing $43 billion plus $5 billion in equity financing.
  • S&P's downgraded Oracle credit rating.To the top of the speculative class (spam margin), rating agencies clearly indicated that AI transition was diluting its original business stability.
  • Impact on job search for studentsThe freeze on recruitment to large factories is expected to increase, the willingness to sponsor the H1B visa is uncertain, and OPT working students are required to assess risks in advance and activate alternative job paths.

---

Why would Oracle want to be laid off? How does the expansion of AI reverse employment?

Oracle's logic is not complicated: In order to win this long-term ticket to AI, human costs must be sacrificed in the short term.

Meanwhile, FY2027 is refinancing. About$40 billion.I don't know. In the face of Wall Street pressure on profitability, compressed human costs have become the most direct control valve.

What concrete impact does this retrenchment have on H1B and OPT students?

Oracle itself is an important sponsor of H1B. Retrenchment entails two types of risks:

I. In-service risk

If you're working H1B in Oracle, you need attention:

  • Immediately after the dismissal, the immigration lawyer was contacted to assess the Bridgen/Cap-exempt opportunities.

II. Risks of active employment

Retrenchment is expected to be transmitted to the entire industry:

  • Recruitment freeze spread: Large factory lay-offs tend to trigger industry winds and small and medium-sized companies tighten HC (headcount).
  • Declining willingness to sponsor visas: Enterprises, under cost pressure, prefer to give preference to candidates without visa sponsorship.

How many days can an OPT be lost of employment during the period? According to USCIS, STEM OPT holders may not exceed the cumulative number of days of unemployment during the period of authorized employer unemployment150 days(Total for the entire OPT+STEM OPT period). The date of separation should be recorded immediately after the dismissal and new authorized employers should be sought as soon as possible to avoid delays.

Financial services, consultancy and relatively robust technology companies (e.g. Capital One, Fidelity, Deloitte, KPMG, etc.) have been recruiting in a more continuous manner during the major plant lay-offs cycle, and some companies have historically been active in sponsoring OPT/H1B.

Oracle FY2026 capital spending exceeded cash flows by $23.7 billion to sustain expansion through large-scale borrowing, and Wall Street's profitability requirements made it necessary to compress operating costs such as manpower simultaneously — that's why S&P downgrades it to the top of the garbage level.

TikTok currently has offices in about 12 cities in the United States, including New York, Austin, Los Angeles and Chicago, and operates through the Joint Venture, which is run by ByteDance and investors from Oracle, Silver Lake, and MGX.

  • Retrenchment begins to take into account the number of days of unemployment on the day, without any buffer

H1B holder:

Of our tutors.Many of them were laid off after three to six months of entry to the post, without an advance layout, which led to extreme passivity within the grace period. In the face of instability, how should students seek employment and evaluate risks?

The stability of a company can be judged by rapid screening of the following dimensions:

Red flag signal (high risk):

  • Retrenchment records for nearly 12 months (available)
  • Positions with high AI replacement rates for content clearance, customer service, operations, etc.
  • The company's recent RTO policy has been significantly tightened (often a precursor to cost cuts)
  • The parent company is under regulatory or political pressure (TikTok / ByteDance ' s structural complexity is in itself a risk factor)

Stability plus sub-items:

Key points

  • The 60-day grace period is still in effect.In accordance with the provisions in force in 2017, visa holders such as H-1B may stay in the United States for up to 60 days after becoming unemployed.
  • Impact on broad visa categoriesIn addition to H-1B, visas E-1, E-2, E-3, H-1B1, L-1, O-1 and TN are also covered by the proposal.
  • Indian holders are at the top of the list.USCIS data show that India ' s birth beneficiaries accounted for 71 per cent of H-1B approval applications in 2024.
  • Chinese students need to be warned.OPT to H1B is the mainstream path, and unemployment triggers an emergency identity risk once the grace period is lifted.

---

What's the H1B 60-day grace period? Which visas does it cover?

In accordance with the current federal legislation in force in 2017, foreign workers holding specific non-immigrant visasAfter unemploymentYou can stay legally in the U.S. 60 consecutive calendar days(or until the expiry of the authorized stay, whichever is the first to arrive, may be used to find a new employer, apply for an identity change or arrange for departure. The same applies to holders of dependent visas (dependant) of the main applicant.

The categories of visas currently protected include:

Type of visaTypical population

L-1Internal redeployment of staff by transnational corporations
O-1Outstanding talent
E-1 / E-2 / E-3Treaty dealer/investor/Australian professional
TNCanadian/Mexico professionals (USMCA)

These 60 days are the key window for many of the workers in the United States "retrenched to find a new job and complete the employer's transfer." Once cancelled, unemployment means that identity becomes illegal almost immediately, unless other legal status is available or USCIS case-by-case discretionary.

---

How far has the 2026 proposal progressed? When will it take effect?

Current proposal in placeAdministrative review phaseThere are still several statutory steps to be taken before the actual landing. According to the information cited by Storyboard 18 and the United States federal legislative process, the timeline is as follows:

PhaseStatusAnnotations

  • The lifting of the grace period meant that a large number of skilled migrants had to leave the country and re-apply for admission.

Main coping strategies (which can be done now):

  • Early maintenance of employer relationsMaintain good communication with HR on the company ' s policy on visa support.

  • Keep an eye on the proposal.Federal public comment periods are important windows that influence the end result and can be submitted through the Regulations.gov.

uscis-w74ax.title: Just now! The new USCIS regulations are in force: not all materials are directly rejected, there is no second chance for a student to apply.
uscis-w74ax.dek: From 5 August 2026 onwards, a full visa/green card application from the USCIS can be refused directly, no additional notice issued, and a student-staying application must be made in one instance.
uscis-w74ax.body:
Since 5 August 2026, the new regulations have been in force: visa and green card applications are incomplete and immigration officers may directly refuse to issue RFE (subsidiary notification) or NOID (notification of intention to refuse). This means that the buffer you once relied on for "required material" has disappeared. I don't know. For students in China who are preparing H1B, green cards, OPT extensions, a single application must be made with zero gaps.

---

Key points

  • Entry into force of new provisions: 5 August 2026This applies to all immigration benefit applications submitted on and after that date, as well as to applications still pending at that date.
  • RFE / NOID no longer "must"Immigration officers have discretion to reject incomplete applications directly by skipping the complementary steps.
  • The impact is extremely wide.H1B, L-1, student visas, family green cards, change/renewal of identity, application for naturalization.
  • "Permitting requests" was clearly struck.According to USCIS, the old policy allows applicants to file incomplete applications to obtain ancillary benefits such as EAD cards, and the new regulations directly block this operation.
  • There's only one thing at the core.: 100% complete pre-submission, no second chance.

---

What did the USCIS 2026 change?

Until 5 August 2026, when the applicant ' s submission is incomplete, USCIS usually follows the following process:

  1. Send RFE(Request for Education, Supplementary Notification)(b) Additional time for the applicant;
  2. Or send NOID (Notice of Intent to Deny, Refusal of Notification of Intent)The applicant is allowed to explain the material gaps.

These two steps gave the applicant a "correct window".The new regulations remove mandatory requirements for this process. According to the USCIS official statement (source: News18 citing Times of India, 6 August 2026), immigration officers can now take a decision of refusal directly if the applicant is unable to prove eligibility at the time of submission.

Key differences:

ItemOld Rules (Biden Age Policy)New regulations (from 5 August 2026)
When materials are incompleteForce RFE / NOID to be sent to fillImmigration officers have discretion to refuse a visa directly.
Opportunities for applicants to correct errorsYes, there is usually an 87-day response window.Insecurity, at the discretion of the official
"Application for a place" is feasible.Existing operating spaceIt's definitely blocked.
Scope of applicationNew applicationsNew applications + 2026-08-05 Pending applications
Policy basisUSCIS Biden Internal GuidanceDHS long-term statutory authority

The official reasons for USCIS include reducing the backlog in the system, improving the efficiency of approvals and combating the use of resources by non-substantive applications.

---

What kind of applications are most at risk? Priority checklist for students

According to the scope of application of the new regulations, the following types of applications have the most direct impact on students staying in China:

Employment visa/status

  • H1B: I-129 Form error, LCA not attached, absence of salary certificate, possible direct rejection
  • L-1: risk of intra-TNC mobility, job description not matching supporting material High
  • OPT / STEM OPT Extension:Form I-765 Material Packages are at risk of rejection of any gaps

Green card class

  • EB-2/EB-3 Green Job Card: I-140 and accompanying labour documentation must be complete
  • Family Green Card: Property security (I-864) documents that were not always RFE high-growth areas are now directly rejected

Student visa/ status maintenance

  • F-1 Extension/change of identity: School DSO-issued materials must match the application

The omission of high-risk materials:

  • Passports not valid enough but not renewed earlier
  • Pay slip / tax return inconsistent with declared income
  • The application form version expired (USCIS regularly updates the form and the old version is directly rejected)
  • Photo does not meet USCIS specifications
  • Supporting documentation is not certified / not accompanied by official translation

---

What's the impact of the new rules on H1B applications?

H1B is the most important working visa route for Chinese students. The impact of the new regulation on H1B is reflected in two phases:

Drawing of lots for registration: Registration itself is relatively small, but the following phase has the greatest impact.

Pettition Submission PhaseThis is the most direct hit point of the new rule. A complete H1B profile usually includes:

  • Form I-129 + H Supplement (all pages must be signed)
  • Labor Condition Application（LCA）, fully matching the position
  • Letter of support from employers(states that the nature of the position is Specialty Election)
  • Certificate of qualification of applicant(degree certificate, report card, evaluation report)
  • Counsel ' s Statement(if any)
  • Cost checks(The amount varies according to the size of the employer)

Under the old rules, the LCA and I-129 job descriptions are slightly inconsistent and may receive RFE requests for explanations.Under the new regulations, immigration officers may directly refuse to sign.

Among the trainees we mentored, RFE was received because of the inconsistency between the LCA duty station and I-129 (cross-state teleworks), and such cases would be directly turned into visa denials under the new rules.Always match every field of LCA with I-129 before submitting.

---

Common problems

When did the new rules come into effect? According to USCIS official guidance, the new regulations Entered into force on 5 August 2026This applies to new applications submitted after that date, as well as to applications still pending at that date (pending).

Is RFE completely canceled? It is not a total cancellation, but no longer a mandatory requirement. Immigration officers "may" continue to issue RFE when deemed appropriate, but are no longer obliged to do so. In ethics, RFE can no longer be expected as a remedy.

If the application was refused directly, could it be re-applied? Resubmission is possible, but the application fee has to be re-paid and the time window may have been missed (e.g. H1B drawing deadline). For H1B, missing a year means waiting for at least another drawing of lots cycle.

How should Chinese students be able to reduce the risk of being directly rejected? The core strategy consists of three: the engagement of licensed immigration lawyers to verify the material individually;2 the use of the latest version of the USCIS official network forms (test form versions and deadlines) before submission;3 the preparation of proactive additional certificates for complex cases (e.g., cross-state remote, academic assessment disputes) rather than RFE.

STEM OPT is affected by the extension request? Affected. STEM OPT applies for extensions through Form I-765, and the new rules also apply. Recommendations advanced 90 days Submit (USCIS allows for the first 90 days of application) to allow for sufficient material preparation time, not to delay until the last few weeks.

---

80-ai-15-ats-fy2o8.dek: Over 80% of the resumes are filtered by algorithms before manual review. It is probably not a question of strength, but of format and keywords.
80-ai-15-ats-fy2o8.body:
Over 80% of curricula vitaeBefore anyone reads it, it has been filtered by the Applicant Tracking System algorithm. For PT / CPT students in North America, whether or not CVs can be first screened by algorithms often determines your fate more than your education or experience. - The good news is, it takes 15 minutes to optimize the ATS, without paying for professional services.

---

Key points

  • 80% + CVBefore arriving at Hiring Manager, it was filtered automatically by ATS (The Economic Times, 2026).
  • ATS doesn't judge potential, only scan.Keywords, job name, skills, educationWhether to match JD.
  • Tables, pictures, multi-column layouts, decorative fonts are the most common ATS killers, and even the best content can be skipped.
  • Each curriculum vitaeMust customise keywords for JDsThe issuance of the same curriculum vitae to all posts was the most common error.
  • Use free tools (e.g. Jobscan) to quickly test ATS compatibility before submission to minimize risk.

---

Why didn't my resume come back? What's the ATS?

Many of the students who were in school had dropped dozens of curricula vitae, which were excellent and matched their experiences, and none of the interviews had been invited. Often the reason is not that you have insufficient qualifications, but that the curriculum vitae is not seen at all.

ATS（Applicant Tracking System）It is an automated software used by enterprises to manage large-volume job applications. Large enterprises, transnational corporations and even medium-sized companies, where a job is often accompanied by hundreds or thousands of applications, are no longer realistic in the first instance. ATS works as follows:

  • Scanning resumesKeywords, job name, skills certification, academic background；
  • Match candidates to JD levelAutomatic ranking；
  • Only first-ranked applications are actually opened by recruiter.
"ATS does not judge personality or potential; it assesses relevance. If the candidate understood this, the chances of obtaining an interview would increase significantly. — Arghya Sarkar, Founder of the Conference Mantra (The Economic Times, 2026)

---

Which resume format will be directly rejected by ATS?

The following are the most common ATS filter traps, where groups of students are particularly vulnerable because of the visual design style of the Chinese curriculum vitae:

Common ErrorsATS ImpactCorrect approach
Multibar Layout / TableParsing order confused, keyword ignoredReplace column with plain text layout
Pictures, Icons, DecorationsATS cannot read graphic contentRemove all graphic elements.
Scan / Photo Version PDFThe whole resume becomes a map, ATS can't read anything.Use PDF or Word for selected text
Non-standard section title.ATS cannot recognize corresponding modulesUse standard English title (see list below)
Same curriculum vitae for all positionsKeywords don't match J.D.Each JD custom keyword
Spelling / Syntax ErrorKeyword misread. Match failed.Grammar check required before submission

Recommended standard section title (ATS identifiable):

  • Professional Summary
  • Work Experience
  • Education
  • Skills
  • Certifications

---

How do you get the resume through ATS in 15 minutes? Step Operation

This is the minimum change, the maximum gain process, certified by the recruitment experts, especially for students in OPT who have had tight time in the search season:

First step (approximately 3 minutes): good reading JD, extraction of high frequency keywords

Opens the JD for the target position to find recurring:

  • Skills (Python, SQL, Tableau, Bloomberg...)
  • Position title (Data Analyst, SDE, Quantitative Researcher...)
  • Authentication / Tools (CFA, AWS, Agile...)
  • verbs for core functions (analyze, development, optimize...)

Step 2 (approximately 3 minutes): Use AI-assisted focus Word

Paste the full JD into ChatGPT and ask, "What are the most important key words in this JD for ATS?"

Note: AI is just a tool,It has to be something that matches your true experience.Do not enter skills that are not available in the curriculum vitae.

Step 3 (approximately 5 minutes): natural integration of keywords into curriculum vitae

Emphasis is placed on:

  • Professional Summary: initial 3-4 sentences, which naturally contain 2-3 core keywords;
  • Work Experience: a description of the function in JD for each bullet, with the synonym replaced by the original JD;
  • Skills Section: A clear listing of the JD-related skills, not stacked without the required skills.

Step four (approximately 2 minutes): replace "description of duties" with "quantified results"

ATS and Hiring Manager both value numbers more. Rewrite examples:

Before rewriting (function description)Recast (quantified results)
Responsible for data analysisAnalyzed 5M+ rows of user data with Python, reducing reporting time by 30%
Assisted in financial modelingBuilt DCF models for 3 M&A deals totaling $200M in transaction value
Managed social media accountsGrew Instagram following by 40% in 6 months, achieving 15% engagement rate
"Recruiters are far more interested in measurable outcomes than generic job responsibilities. Numbers tell a stronger story." —— Arghya Sarkar，Recruitment Mantra（The Economic Times，2026）

Step 5 (approximately 2 minutes): ATS compatibility test with free tools

Use before submitting Jobscan(jobscan.co) Upload CV + JD, get ATS matching score report. Target fraction recommended in 70% or moreResubmitted.

---

Special attention for students: OPT/CPT Additional pits in job search

Students in the OPT / H1B stage also have several special mined areas on the curriculum vitae:

  • Do not add "need H1B Sponsonship" to the resume title.: such keywords may trigger some of the company's ATS filter rules, if specified, in a dedicated entry box in the Cover Letter or job search platform;
  • Full name of school.: for example, "University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign" instead of the abbreviation UIUC, ATS matches the full string;
  • GPA uniform format: Write "GPA: 3.8/4.0", ATS sensitive to format;
  • Apprenticeship / Full name in English for companies with scientific experience: To avoid the failure of interpretation in Chinese or abbreviations.

---

Common problems

What's the difference between the ATS CV and the CV? ATS CVs give priority to ensuring machine readability: individual text, standard section titles, keywords are highly compatible with JD; the CVs may be more visual, but visual design is less subdivisions before ATS.

Should I write a new curriculum vitae for every job? There is no need to rewrite from the beginning, but core keywords and substantive Summer must be customised for each JD. Usually 20-30% of the keyword content is changed, and the ATS matching score is significantly increased.

PDF or Word? Both are available, and the key is that text must be optional (non-photo/scanned). If JD or the application system does not have a special description, the PDF of the selected text is a safer option that prevents the format from being unwieldy when Word opens.

Free ATS testing tools? The free version of Jobscan provides a limited number of matching analyses per month, data from real ATS system logic and results are of reference value. It is suggested that cross-validation be combined with multiple tools rather than relying on a single platform score.

How can it be written in ATS, friendly English? Recast the project into English bullet in accordance with the STAR principles (Situation / Task / Action / Research), with a focus on quantifiable Result (number, scale, impact), with skills names consistent with JD. Many of the 300+ participants we mentored had internships from their home countries, which were rewritten and successfully interviewed by Goldman Sachs, Meta, Amazon, etc.

ai-16-lzrzb.body:
In 2026, four scientific and technological companies, Oracle, Amazon, Cloudflare and Block, all referred to "AI" in their vacancy announcements, but according to the latest analysis of Trading Platforms, what they call "AI layoffs" actually points to completely different commercial decisions. Understanding the differences is crucial for North American students who are seeking jobs or preparing to jump — also known as "AI layoffs" — but the level of risk and the job-seeking strategy are very different.

---

Key points

  • By mid-July 2026, 156,975 jobs had been lost in the global science and technology industry, nearly 60 per cent of which were related to AI-driven restructuring(Source: Trading Platforms, based on TrueUp, TechCrunch, Layoffs.fyi and several US WarN databases).
  • The Oracle staff was downsized by 25,254 and net profits surged by 95 per cent to $6.13 billion over the same period— The savings from layoffs are directed to AI infrastructure, not because AI has replaced jobs.
  • Amazon's downsized over 17,000 people. It's basically organizational flattening.During the same period, a total of $716.9 billion was collected during the 2025 fiscal year, with a planned capital expenditure of up to $200 billion.
  • Claudflare and Block's retrenchment is closer to "Ai's direct replacement.": The use of the Claudflare internal AI tool has increased by 600% in three months, and the Block leadership has made it clear that AI has been able to take on a "substantial part of the job" of its staff.

Oracle and Amazon layoffs, more likeRedistribution of financial resourcesAnd not AI technology directly replaces labor.

  • While 25,254 jobs were cut, net profits surged from 95 per cent to $6.13 billion in the same year.

The logic of Amazon:

  • There were more than 17,000 staff reductions, with the core objective being "simplified organizational structure" (i.e., reduced management levels).
  • During the same period, a total of $716.9 billion was collected in 2025 and the AI capital expenditure plan for 2026 was announced at $200 billion.
  • Retrenchment is a budget release for large-scale AI construction, not because AI has replaced these staff members.

Meaning for students to seek employment: Such companies continue to recruit a large number of technical personnel for AI infrastructure, cloud computing and data engineering. Cloudflare and Block represent one.It's a much more alarming pattern of layoffs.• The leadership clearly linked the enhancement of the capacity of the AI tool directly to personnel reductions.

  • The company named this lay-off a transition to an "agentic AI-first operating model".
  • Use of internal AI tools increased by more than 600 per cent in just three months.
  • It's worth noting.Claudflare had previously publicly advocated the expansion of the recruitment of interns and claimed that AI should "enhanced" rather than replace "staff" — but a few months later this massive staff reduction was announced, with clear inconsistencies in the narrative.

What happened to Block:

  • With a reduction of 4,000, the leadership has made it clear that AI is now able to deal with a "substantial part" of the work performed by the laid-off staff.
  • This was the most straightforward of the four companies — AI alternatives were officially recognized.

Analysis of Trading Platforms suggests that: Only a relatively small number of companies currently have AI systems that can truly take over a large amount of work in a scale scenario. Most of the staff reductions in 2026 were essentially "preventive cost cuts" to finance AI infrastructure — rather than direct evidence that AI automation has replaced human jobs on a large scale.

---

  • Software Engineering (SDE) - AIS Product Direction: The demand for engineers to build the AAI product back and forth and to integrate the API continues to grow.

Caution is needed:

  • The leadership of the company has publicly indicated that AI could replace the specific work content of the current position.
  • The number of AI tools used by the company jumped significantly over the same period (e.g. 600 per cent increase in Cloudflare).
  • The team works primarily on standardization, processization and duplication (most easily taken over by agentic AI).

A key diagnostic framework: Ask yourself -- is this company building new things with AI? The former is an opportunity for job seekers, while the latter is a risk signal.
