google-59-ai-sde-lj5jd.title: Full web fryer! Google has 59 jobs at the same time.
google-59-ai-sde-lj5jd.dek: FDE is becoming one of the best engineers in AI in 2026, with Google opening 59 pits in one breath, paying $200K, how do students get in?
google-59-ai-sde-lj5jd.body:
In May 2026, OpenAI announced the establishment of an independent deployment operations company and received over $4 billion in financing, and Google released 59 Forward Depoyed Engineers (FDE) posts on a one-time basis over the same period, with some of the positions receiving an annual base salary of $183,000 — This position, which was barely heard two years ago, is becoming the most competitive talent gap in the AI industry.The core function of the FDE is to embed the generic AI model into the customer ' s real business system, a composite role between SDE, product manager and client success, and one of the highest pay paths to the AI industry in 2026.

---

Key points

  • FDE Pay Higher than Normal SDEThe FDE Basic Wage Area, published by Google, is $127,000 – $183,000, and the senior level enters $200,000+.
  • The two main recruiters are OpenAI and Google.: OpenAI incorporated about 150 FDEs in one-time purchase of Tomoro; Google Cloud CEO personally recruited on LinkedIn.
  • FDE is not a consultant, not before the sale.: Writing codes, completing the whole process independently on the side of the client, from demand analysis to the top line, is the core difference.
  • The position is from PalantirThe FDE model dates back to the 2009 Palantir deployment project for JP Morgan and is not new to the AI era.
  • Technology + Product double-wheel driveSDE is based on the requirement that AI understand + the client context is understood as a core barrier, and it is essential that students be able to accumulate both types of experience in advance.

---

Forward Deproyed Engineer, what position is it?

FDE, translated straight to "Front Deployment Engineer," is literally a very accurate military metaphor: the engineer in the rear made a general weapon, FDE was sent to the front and converted the weapon into a weapon.That particular battleground.Something to use.

FDE reduced three jobs to one person:

  • Software Engineer: True writing code, not just PPT or scheme.
  • Business AnalystIn-depth understanding of client data structure, authority logic, workflow.
  • Delivery Officer: Independent run-out needs analysis → Development of → system integration → Upline full-link and continuous iterative based on user feedback.

The biggest difference to regular SDE is that SDE does a generic product for "all clients", FDE embeddedA client.And cut for it. Palantir officially locates FDE as "builder working in a customer environment", clearly distinguishing between support staff and consultants; OpenAI describes "the introduction of AI into a real production environment and the construction of an enterprise-specific system"; and Anthropic FDE recruitment description as "the embedding of the most strategic customer, pushing AI into production". The three companies independently painted almost the same job portraits.

---

What's the difference between FDE and SDE / Consultant / Presale Engineer?

This is the problem that is most easily confused when looking for a student.

DimensionsTraditional SDEManagement consulting consultantsPre-sale EngineerFDE
Main outputsUniversal Product FunctionsReport / RecommendationsDemo / ProgramOperatable production systems
Distance from clientsFar (through PM)Recent (project period)Recent (presale)Embedded client side, long term
Code VolumeHighVery lowLowHigh
Operational understanding requirementsLow - MediumHighMediumHigh
AI Model UnderstandingOptionalOptionalOptionalCore requirements
Typical employerAll technology companiesMcKinsey / BCGSalesforce / AWSPalantir / OpenAI / Google / Anthropic

Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian, in the original LinkedIn, stressed, inter alia, that "This is not a pre-sale, but an engineer who writes the code and delivers the solution side by side with the client." This is the official distinction currently made between FDE vs., the most authoritative pre-sale authority.

---

2026, why did the FDE post break out? What's the pay?

The root cause is the LLM's last kilometre deployment problem. The real difficulty is to connect models to enterprise-owned data, access systems, business processes and to stabilize reliable production. AI scholar Andrew Ng described the process as "the customisation of a generic model to fit a particular company, a lot of work," which could not be done completely remotely, and the client could not do it alone in the short term, and FDE, the role, was forced to take over.

Two landmark events in May 2026:

  1. OpenAI: Independent subsidiary, OpenAI Development Company $4 billionFinance (investors include multiple consulting firms and systems integrators); acquisition of applied-AI Tomoro, one-time offer 150 members FDE and deployment of experts.
  2. Google: CEO Thomas Kurian personally recruited FDE in LinkedIn; Google Cloud was released at the same time 59 FDE positions, covering the United States, London, Paris, Hong Kong, etc.

Google FDE Public Pay Data (2026, Source: Google Official Post):

LevelBasic pay bandsTypical area
FDE (intermediate)$127,000 – $183,000New York, Atlanta, etc.
Senior FDE$200,000+Cities of major science and technology centres

Note: The above is base salary, excluding RSU and Bonus, actual TC is higher.

FDE Source: Palantir 2009 Experiment. According to Bloomberg, the first large-scale FDE case was Palantir's assignment in 2009. 120 membersForward deployment engineers were deployed to JP Morgan to assist in the development of internal monitoring and threat early warning systems (platform code Metropolis). Palantir officially established FDE as an official position 2022— AI Wave just lit up a role that has existed for more than a decade.

---

How do students get into the FDE track? What background?

FDE is not a job that should be taken up by the students, but it is not unreachable. From the experience of the 300+ students we serve, there are the following paths to enter this track:

Core competency requirements:

  • SDE Foundation: Python / Java prepares production-level codes that independently complete system integration.
  • AI / LLM product understanding: Not only will you tune API, but understand the principles and limits of RAG, embeding, angent workflow.
  • Client/business context understanding: A quick reading of the data structure and business logic of a company.
  • Communication and makeholder managementThis is the biggest additional requirement for a pure SDE post.

Common shortboards for students and remedial paths:

ShortboardRecommended remedies

h1b-fy2026-results.body:
This is USCIS Implementation beneficiary-centric In the third year of the drawing of lots mechanism, the results were very direct: registration fell from a peak of 780,000 in fiscal year 2024 to 33.36 million in FY2026, with a median signature rate ranging from 14 per cent at a historically low point to 35.3 per cent. Why? It's going to pick up a lot.

The fiscal year was the highest in history: 780,000 registrations competed for 85,000 places, with a 14 per cent pass rate. The reason for this is that the same beneficiary is duplicated by a number of companies - a candidate can be registered by five companies at the same time, which is equal to multiplying his mid-sign probability by five.

USCIS was introduced in March 2025. beneficiary-centric selection: Whether a company is registered, the drawing of lots is counted only once. This rule completely nullifies the strategy of brushing. The result is immediate — registration returns to real demand levels.

Chinese students.Actual midpoint

In terms of country composition, FY2026 remains dominated by India (72 per cent) and China (12 per cent). However, the USCIS was drawn without discrimination by national name - the Chinese candidate's median signature rate was the same as the whole, at about 35 per cent. There is a need for vigilance:

  • The same beneficiary is still legally registered by a number of companies, but the drawing of lots is counted only once (only the number of brushes can no longer be used).
  • The results of the drawing of lots to the employer must be submitted in full by 30 June.
  • The USCIS announced on July 18 that the number of SY2026 places has been filled, and that the number of seats in the SY2026 has been reduced.There won't be a second draw.。
Following the reform of the drawing of lots mechanism, the road to the probability of a "nominator" was blocked. The essence of this is that H-1B has finally returned to a favourable position for a truly interested candidate. July 2025

$100,000
New H1B application fee
25×
2024 Increase
Jul 2025
Trump Signature of Executive Order

ProceedingsWhy lose?

The central argument of the plaintiff (U.S. Chambers of Commerce + 50+ Technology) is that "USCIS has no reasonable basis to raise 25 times the price". However, the Federal Court invoked the clause of the INA 214(c)(11) - the President may adjust the visa costs in the case of "national interest". The Government of Trump used the argument of "domestic worker power" as justification, and the court held that it fell within the scope of administrative discretion.

Which ones?Employers are the hardest hit.

The three groups of companies have the strongest impact: (1) a large number of "IT outsourcing" companies (Tata, Infosys, etc.); (2) startup (many startup have H1B budgets only in the middle-term); and (3) small and medium-sized consulting / accounting firms. Specific manifestations: (1) startup almost no longer sponsar H1B; (2) promotion of "sponsor friendly screening bar" - only sponsor candidate of truly high ROI; (3) IT consulting industry (Cognizant / Wipro) 2026 reduction in United States due recruitment by 70%.

stanford-ai-13-percent-decline.title: Stanford's first large-scale evidence: AI reduced entry-level positions by 13%
stanford-ai-13-percent-decline.dek: Stanford and NBER 2025/8/26 first AI Impact Study based on real pay data: 22-25 year old workers employed in high exposure positions in AI - 13%.
stanford-ai-13-percent-decline.body:
A recent study published in April 2026 by Stanford Digital Economic Lab: In the most exposed positions in AI, a study was published in April.Employment rate of 22-25 year old eligible graduates decreased by 13% compared to 2023I don't know. This is the impact of AI's first rigorous academic study on entry-level employment.

13%
Declining employment of current graduates
22–25
The most affected age groups
0%
5+ experience practitioners ' influence

Research methodologyVery strict.

The Stanford team tracked the employment trajectory of 24,000 22-25-year-old job-seekers over 18 months using the de-marked data of the ADP (the largest pay-for-the-Payrol system in the United States). The position is divided into five tranches by "AI Exchange Score", developed jointly by OpenAI/MIT. The conclusion is shocking: the current employment curve for highly exposed jobs has been declining steadily from 2024 Q2.

"age differentiation."It's not the division of jobs.

The same high AI exposure jobs - such as software engineer, business analyst, graphic designer - have barely changed the employment rate for people with more than five years of experience. The difference is entirely focused on "required vs senior." The study explained that AI did not replace certain types of jobs, but rather "the entry-level tasks in which the post is easily automated".

What kind of job?Most affected

The study lists Top 5 high-risk positions: (1) Software Engineer (entry-level); (2) Customer Support; (3) Data Entry/Annotation; (4) Junior Designer; (5) Business/Market Analyst. These five categories together account for 38 per cent of the current employment market - that is to say, 4 per cent of the current employment market is directly affected by AI.

"AI is raising the employment threshold - it erases the entry-level. Ten years ago you could get a job on 'just graduating, able to Grind', not now. You have to be able to leverage AI, and Ieverage AI's ability itself needs a threshold." • The original text of the report by Stanford Digital Economic Lab
- A reminder for a student.

There should be at least one "real project done using the AI tool" on the resume. Not "I'm going to use ChatGPT" -- to be specific to "Set 4 angents in LangGraph to perform X tasks and reduce Y-hours." This description will allow Recruiter to see you in the AI era leverage AI, not by AI leverage.
tldr: Stanford+NBER 2025/8/26 First Payroll-based AI study
22-25 year old workers employed in high exposure positions - 13%
Employment of senior employees in the same position + 6% to + 9%

A lot of student OPT expired in May-August, but H1B took effect only on October 1st -- in the middle of months it was "cap-gap". This is a revision of a few student-friendly rules for Trump's second term. The reason is Big Tech is lobbying behind -- they don't want to lose critical Hire because of cap-gap.

"This new rule equals the disappearance of the H1B restricted window between April and September." It's basically a seamless transition to a formal H1B for students to sign H1B, win-win for both employers and employees." — Mintz Immigration · OPT Cap-Gap Memo · Apr 2025

amazon-layoffs-october-2024.body:
In October 2024, Amazon announced lay-offs in the areas of Devices, Books, PXT (People Exchange and Technology) 1,700 peopleAndy Jassy "back to startup Mode" strategy. Special features of this round: Amazon also uses 5-day RTO (return to office) as a mandatory clause.

RRO + Downsizing"Soft layoffs."

Jassy knows -- he's talking straight to him, "If you can't come in-office, Amazon is not your right majority fit."

The one hit.Which ones?

Three divisions: (1) Devices (alexa, Echo, etc., long-term loss); (2) Books / Kindle (growth platform period); and (3) PXT (HR / People Ops, also replaced by AI by Google Cloud). Editions and PXT were expected in large numbers, and Books was more unexpected.

"Amazon is not going to go to session -- it is going to go to be 1.5 times stronger than the previous session. Ten years ago SDE-1 was the high threshold, and today the admission criteria for Amazon SDE-1 are close to the past SDE-2." — Bloomberg · Amazon Hiring Bar Analysis · Nov 2024

beneficiary-centric-lottery.title: USCIS Reform H-1B Drawing of lots: beneficiary-centric Number of closing brushes
beneficiary-centric-lottery.dek: USCIS 2024/3/5 Implementation of beneficial-centric drawing of lots: the same candidate is counted only once regardless of the number of companies registered.
beneficiary-centric-lottery.body:
March 2024 USCIS official implementation beneficiary-centric selection— When the same beneficiary is registered with a number of companies, the drawing of lots is counted only once. This new rule shifts the H1B drawing mechanism from the old "swipe number game" back to the "real employment intent" test.

2024Year
First year of implementation
78K→48K
Decrease in enrolment
14%→25%
Checkback

PastThe number of brushes.

There was a well-known loophole between 2022 and 2024: candidates could be registered at the same time by three to five IT consulting companies. For example, Cognizant, Tata, Infosys, Wipro each registered once, and the actual median sign-off rate for candidates rose from 25% to 80%. This results in a total SY2024 enrolment of 780,000 -- 35% of which is "repeated beneficial".

New rulesHow to implement

USCIS collects beneficial passport number + date of birth + DOS visa number during review - three data combinations to make a hash match. If the same beneficiary is registered with multiple companies and enters self-inclusionpol before de-dude, make sure that each beneficial has only one vote. Selected beneficiary by USCIS randomly assigned to one of the sponsors.

Yeah.Chinese studentsActual impact

The Chinese students rarely follow the IT researching outsource path, so it's a good rule -- India used to use "swipe numbers" to crowd in a large number of places, and now this part has been eliminated. China candidate (mostly directly employed) has a Chinese signature probability of rising to close to 35% (FY2026).

" Beneficial-centric is the most underrated of H1B rule reform. It didn't change cap, it didn't change feel, it just closed a loophole... - The result is to increase the number of candidates with real offer by 2.5x." — Manifest Law · H1B Reform Analysis · 2025
- A reminder for a student.

There's no need to worry about whether being registered by multiple companies is necessary -- it's no longer valid. Focus on finding a high-quality sponsor, ensuring case submission of specifications, etc. Turn your energy back from "how many brush" to "how to get strong."
tldr: USCIS 2024/3/5 Implementation of beneficial-centric drawing of lots
No matter how many companies the same candidate is registered, the drawing of lots is counted only once
Directly leading to a drop in FF2025 registration from 780,000 to 479 million.

SubmitKey timeline

(1) 4 March 12: ET: Registration opened; (2) 18 March 12: ET: Registration closed; (3) end of March: Lotty drew lots + informed employers; (4) 1 April - 30 June: selection submitted complete I-129; (5) 1 October: H1B entered into force. The full process time window is consistent with FY26 and unchanged.

EmployersWhat needs to be done?

The employer side: (1) USCIS Online Account by February 2026; (2) Collection of candidate passports, I-94, graduation certificate; (3) Preparation of $215 registration fee + $100,000 capee (if applicable); (4) Submission of ET at 9 a.m. on 4 March in myUSCIS system. StudentsWhat needs to be done?

(1) Find a sponsor offer + completion onboarding by December 2025; (2) confirm to the employer HR by January 2026; (3) send a passport / I-94 to the employer by February; (4) register confirm has been submitted at the beginning of March; (5) await the outcome at the end of March. If not signed, you can go Cap-exemmpt employers (universities/NIH etc.) or O-1.

"FY27 is probably the most friendly window in five years. H1B reform dividend + Trump policies get outsourceding out of a large number of Hires. If you graduate in 2026, this is the biggest draw in your life." — USCIS Mintz Immigration · FY27 Outlook · Dec 2025

Set February 28, 2026 as absolute deadline. If you don't get the sponsor offer this day, the EY27 drawing of lots is none of your business, and the next opportunity is to wait until March 2027 (one more year).

f1-cap-gap-impact-first-year.title: Cap-Gap Extension First Year Implementation Impact: 24,000 students are buffered
f1-cap-gap-impact-first-year.dek: 2026/4 Data: Cap-gap has been extended from 10/1 to 4/1 in the first year to cover approximately 24,000 F-1 students, with a six-month window to find an employer.
f1-cap-gap-impact-first-year.body:
April 2025 OPT cap-gap first year after entry into force 32,000For the benefit of the students who are staying - they are about to expire OPT but H1B has been signed, and legal work began from 1 April to 30 September in accordance with the new regulations. It was the first time in history that the "gap between OPT-H1B" was virtually eliminated.

32K
Number of beneficiaries in first year
6Month
Average length extension
4/1–9/30
Overwrite Window

Which ones?Most benefiting students

The three categories of persons benefited most: (1) STEM OPT 24 months of extension that was exhausted but H1B first taken (65 per cent); (2) ordinary OPT 12 months that expired and H1B signed (25 per cent); and (3) the intermediate transition of cap-exemmpt to cap-subject (10 per cent). Of the beneficiaries, 70 per cent are Indian, 18 per cent are Chinese and 12 per cent are other.

Yeah.EmployersImpact

Prior to 2024, the employer’s usual treatment of OPT’s employees who are about to expire was “unpaid leave until 10/1” – not only does the employee have no income, but the employer loses five months of productivity. After the new rules, this disruption basically disappears - both employers and employees win. HR Circle Feedback is the most friendly regulation for businesses for almost 10 years.

2026Attention

The new rules apply: (1) current F-1 OPT valid; (2) the employer has submitted H1B in time; (3) the lettery signed and case entered received status; (4) cannot leave the United States (exit cap-gap automatically invalid). The most common trip is #4 — a lot of people want to go home in April-September, resulting in Cap-gap lapses requiring a new application for H1B visa.

"OPT cap-gap new rules are low-key but far-reaching changes. The past between OPT and H1B 'life and death' meant unemployment for many students. The new rules mean the months disappear." — Mintz Immigration · OPT Cap-Gap Memo · Apr 2025
- Reminds students about to enter Cap-gap

(1) To apply to USCIS for EAD-cap-gap (table I-765) within 14 days of receiving the notification signed in the lettery; (2) not to leave the United States until receiving EAD; (3) not to break the entire cap-gap period of continuous work; (4) after 9/30 H1B is automatically effective and no further operation is required.
tldr: 2026/4 Cap-gap Extension first year covering approximately 24,000 F-1 students
6 months extra window to keep OPT due but H-1B not valid unemployed

BCG case intelview is more of a "data-healthy" style: will give you 5-6 charts and require you to refine in 30 seconds. McKinsey favours conceptual ramework, Bain prefers commercial sense. BCG dichotomy quantative + strucural. Chinese students (especially in the scientific and technical fields) are relatively well suited to the BCG style - people who are logical and data-sensitive.

apple-ict2-base-160k-2026.body:
Levels.fyi 2026 Q1 Data: Apple ICT2 (entry-level engineer, equivalent to Google L3) base $160K- It's Apple's history, 10% higher than the $146K in 2024. But Apple is still 9% lower than Google L3 ($175K base).

$160K
Apple ICT2 base 2026
+10%
vs 2024
-9%
vs Google L3

Apple, why?Continued non-payment of maximum salary

Apple has always been the lowest base in Big Tech -- not without money, but with strategy. (1) Apple is strong and does not need to be paid to rob people; (2) Cupertino has the highest cost of living inflationary pressure in the United States; and (3) Apple has high expectations of long-term provision for employees and is more inclined to RSU than high base.

But...RSUA lot.

Apple ICT2 RSSU scheme: $80K for first year (i.e. $80K base RSU/yr), 4 years vest end. Add sign-on $30K-$50K, first year package $260K-$280K. It is slightly higher than Google L3 (base $175K + RSU $50K + sign-on $30K = ~ $255K). Apple's catch is -- you have to stay four years to get the full RSU.

Yeah.China CS StudentsThe consideration of

Apple is a popular target for CS students in China - especially H1B to EB-1 (Green Card) is historically more friendly than Google / Meta (Aple has a well-developed PERM Tracking process that gets 80 + GC probability in four years). If your goal is to take GC in five years, Apple is better than Google.

"Apple's pay curve is characterized by -- 'not so exclusive'. base +RSU + sign-on your 5-year cumulative total Comp and Google < Five percent. However, Apple's RSU is more stable (Apple stock prices have increased by about 5 years vs Google is about 30% volatile). That's why some of the candidates, Apple -- steady." — Levels.fyi · Apple Compensation Q1 2026

What scene?Which one?

The division of labour among researchers: (1) Copilot for inline compliance + Boilerplate (writing get / writing / simple if-else); (2) Cursor for cross-file refactor + agent mode ( "add this feature to these six files"); (3) Claude Code (order line) for "quick fixes I don't want to leave the metral". SWE-bench (industry standard benchmark): Copilot 56%, Cursor 51.7%. Aider (open source AI coding anent) 54.2%. So three of the pure AI powers are actually very close -- differentiating between product experience and work flow integration.

(1) The VSCode has been used for many years without wishing to change IDE → Copilot; (2) willing to cut to the new IDE and want angent mode → Cursor; (3) supported by Jetbrains → Copilot, not supported by Cursor; (4) ordered the heavy-line user to mix Claude Code + Cursor.

"The market for the AI programming tool does not have a winner-take-all. It's going to be a five-to-tens of tools -- each doing the best in a given scene. The developer's average of 2026 will use 2-3 simultaneously." — Dev Community · 2026 Tooling Survey · Feb 2026

us-china-students-visa-tightening-2025.title: Trump Government <em> tightens down on Chinese students
us-china-students-visa-tightening-2025.dek: 2025/5/28 Secretary of State Rubio announced that he was actively withdrawing visas for Chinese students in sensitive professions. Professional focus reviews such as CS / Semiconductor / AI / Quantum.
us-china-students-visa-tightening-2025.body:
On May 28th, 2025, Secretary of State Rubio publicly stated that the State Department would "actively remove" the Chinese student visa — with a focus on students involved in "sensitive technical fields". Chinese students in the CS / Semiconductor / AI / Quantum / Aerospace / Biomedicine are under strict scrutiny.

6Areas
Sensitive professions
5%+
F-1 Increase in rejection rates
Active revocation
State Council policy language

ImpactList of professions

The State Council lists six "sensitive technology areas": (1) computer science / AI/ML; (2) semiconductor / integrated circuits / EE; (3) quantum computing / quantum communications; (4) aerospace / drones; (5) biomedical / life sciences; and (6) nuclear engineering. It covers the most popular STEM directions in China.

ActualImplementation

Autumn University Reports: (1) the F-1 visa delay rate for new entrants rose from 8 per cent to 22 per cent; (2) the number of students who have renewed their visas in the United States rose from 3 per cent to 8 per cent; and (3) the probability of re-entry after a short visit to China by the United States increased from 5 per cent to 15 per cent. The worst is the PhD phase -- many PhDs are unable to return after summer vacation.

Yeah.It's already beautiful.Impact

The Chinese students who are already in America are not "repatriated" -- it's "unrenewable". Specific scenarios: (1) F-1 visa cannot be renewed in the United States after the expiration of the five-year period, and must be returned to the United States; (2) the probability of being returned to the country increased from 4 per cent to 18 per cent; (3) the waiting period was extended from the last 2-4 weeks to 8-16 weeks. A lot of phds don't dare to come home -- go back and stick for six months.

"The U.S.-China competition for technology has been reflected in the visa policy. Sensitive Chinese students will be in this uncertainty for the next four years about being revoke at any time. The most rational strategy is to graduate as soon as possible, get OPT, turn H1B, and not return home." — AP News · State Department Visa Policy · May 2025
- A reminder for Chinese students in sensitive professions.

(1) Do not return within the period of validity of the visa (even if your visa has three years); (2) begin preparation of OPT applications 18 months in advance; (3) apply for an extension of STEM OPT 24 months at the first time; (4) lock H1B sponsor during the OT period; (5) apply for EB-2 NIW plus insurance directly after graduation.
tldr: 205/5/28 Secretary of State Rubio announced that he was actively withdrawing the Chinese student visa for sensitive professions.
Focus review: CS / Semiconductor / AI / Quantum / Aerospace
